title: Fire Service Authority
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to affirm the legal authority of the Stickney Fire Department and the individual
members.
POLICY
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to limit its members to only exercise the authority granted
to them by law.
While the Stickney Fire Department recognizes the authority of members granted to them, members are
encouraged to use sound discretion in the exercise of their authority, and this department does not
tolerate abuse of authority.
When exercising their authority, members shall observe and comply with every person’s clearly
established rights under the United States and Illinois Constitutions.
I. POWERS
A. ORGANIZATIONAL POWERS: This department is authorized by Illinois law to perform fire
suppression and related services including, but not limited to, the following (65 ILCS 5/11-
6-1 et seq.):
1. Fire prevention and fire code enforcement
2. Fire suppression services
3. Fire cause and origin investigation
4. Emergency Medical Services (EMS)
5. Specialized rescue services
6. Technical rescue services
B. FIREFIGHTER POWERS: Firefighters are commissioned members of this department and
are authorized to exercise the following authority:
1. Participate in a wide range of emergency and rescue activities, including EMS,
extrication and heavy rescue.
2. Perform fire suppression duties, including the suppression of structural, aircraft,
marine, wildland and other types of fires.
3. Investigate the cause and origin of fires.

4. Collect and preserve evidence when a fire is of a suspicious origin.
5. Perform specialty services, including hazardous materials response, technical
rescue, water rescue and additional services as authorized by the Fire Chief
6. Provide fire code enforcement inspection and plan review services.
7. Provide public education and fire prevention activities and services.
II. SUPERVISORY AUTHORITY
A. Any chief officer may relieve a member under his/her command from duty when, in
his/her judgment, an offense committed is sufficiently serious to warrant immediate
action. A report of such action shall be made immediately through the appropriate
channels to the Fire Chief or designee followed by written documentation of the charges,
in accordance with department rules/ regulations and policies.
B. All such processes shall also comply with applicable collective bargaining agreements.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Firefighter Code Of Ethics
body:
PURPOSE:
To set forth for all members and employees of the Stickney Fire Department an articulated code of ethics
and conduct which encompasses and describes expectations of behavior and conduct, both on duty and
off duty.
POLICY
All members of the Stickney Fire Department must be fully aware of the ethical responsibilities of their
position and must strive constantly to live up to the highest possible standards of professional policing.
Each member of the Stickney Fire Department is required to abide by the Code of Ethics.
I. RESPONSIBILITIES
A. This agency will maintain, periodically review, and update a code of ethics.
B. Each employee (current and new hires) will be required to read and sign a copy of the
code of ethics to signify that the standards of conduct set forth therein are understood
and will be followed (Appendix A). The signed copy of the code of ethics will be maintained
in the employee’s personnel file. The employee will be provided with a photocopy.
C. Failure to abide by the conditions and standards as set forth in the Code of Ethics will be
considered a violation of the Rules of Conduct and may result in disciplinary action as
provided in the Rules and Regulations of the department.
D. The code of ethics will be regarded as guiding principles for daily ethical living.
E. Employees will provide information in a timely manner to their supervisor or a command
level officer when improper practices are suspected or known to have taken place.
II. FIREFIGHTER CODE OF ETHICS
As a firefighter and member of the Stickney Fire Department, my fundamental duty is to
serve the community; to safeguard and preserve life and property against the elements
of fire and disaster; and maintain a proficiency in the art and science of fire engineering.
I will uphold the standards of my profession, continually search for new and improved
methods and share my knowledge and skills with my contemporaries and successors.
I will not allow personal feelings, nor danger to self, deter me from my responsibilities
as a firefighter.

I will at all times, respect the property and rights of all men and women, the laws of my
community and my country, and the chosen way of life of my fellow citizens.
I recognize the badge of my office as a symbol of public faith, and I accept it as a public
trust to be held so long as I am true to the ethics of the fire service. I will never use my
official position to obtain advantages or favors for myself, my friends or family.
I will constantly strive to achieve the objectives and ideals, dedicating myself to my
chosen profession–saving of life, fire prevention and fire suppression.
As a member of the Stickney Fire Department, I accept this self-imposed and selfenforced obligation as my responsibility.
III. TRAINING
A. The training officer is responsible for providing ongoing training in ethics, integrity,
prevention of impropriety, and professional standards for all levels of the department.
B. All personnel will receive ethics training every two years.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Policy & Procedure Manual
body:
PURPOSE:
The Policy Manual of the Stickney Fire Department is hereby established and shall be referred to as the
Policy & Procedure Manual or the manual. The manual is a statement of the current policies, rules and
guidelines of this department. All members are expected to conform to the provisions of this manual.
All prior and existing policies, manuals, orders and regulations that are in conflict with this manual are
revoked, except to the extent that portions of the existing manuals, procedures, orders and other
regulations that have not been included herein shall remain in effect where they do not conflict with the
provisions of this manual.
POLICY:
Except where otherwise expressly stated, the provisions of this manual shall be considered as guidelines.
It is recognized that fire and rescue work is not always predictable, and circumstances may arise that
warrant departure from these guidelines. It is the intent of this manual to be viewed using an objective
standard, taking into consideration the sound discretion entrusted to the members of this department
under the circumstances reasonably available at the time of any incident.
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to make any immediate changes to policy and procedure
in accordance with supporting the operations, mission, vision, and values of the Stickney Fire Department.
The establishment of General Orders is management’s prerogative, but employee participation may be
sought in the development of those policies at the discretion of the Fire Chief, or his designee.
I. DEFINITIONS
A. The following words and terms shall have these assigned meanings throughout the Policy
Manual, unless it is apparent from the content that they have a different meaning.
1. Adult - Any person 18 years of age or older.
2. Department/SFD - The Stickney Fire Department.
3. Fire Code - The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 101 Life Safety Code,
2000 Edition (425 ILCS 25/9; 41 Ill. Adm. Code 100.7).
4. Firefighter - Those members, regardless of rank, who perform fire suppression
duties as part of their primary duties as sworn or commissioned members of the
Stickney Fire Department. Firefighter also means fire protection personnel.
5. Manual - The Stickney Fire Department Policy Manual.
6. May - Indicates a permissive, discretionary or conditional action.

7. Member - Any person who is employed or appointed by the Stickney Fire
Department, including firefighters, reserve firefighters, non-sworn members, and
volunteers.
8. On-duty - Member status during the period when he/she is actually engaged in
the performance of his/her assigned duties.
9. Order - A written or verbal instruction issued by a superior.
10. Rank - The title of the classification held by a firefighter.
11. Shall or will - Indicates a mandatory action.
12. Should - Indicates a generally required or expected action, absent a rational basis
for failing to conform.
13. Supervisor - A person in a position of authority regarding hiring, transfer,
suspension, promotion, discharge, assignment, reward or discipline of other
department members, directing the work of other members or having the
authority to adjust grievances. The term "supervisor" may also include any person
(e.g., firefighter-in-charge, lead or senior worker) given responsibility for the
direction of the work of others without regard to a formal job title, rank or
compensation.
14. Village - The Village of Stickney.
II. AUTHORITY
A. The Fire Chief shall be considered the ultimate authority for the content and adoption of
the provisions of this manual and shall ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state
and local laws.
B. The Fire Chief or the authorized designee is authorized to issue General Orders, which
shall modify those provisions of the manual to which they pertain. General Orders shall
remain in effect until such time as they may be permanently incorporated into the
manual.
III. POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL FORMAT
A. The policy format will be used on the initial page of each order.
1. The heading includes:
a) Order Number
b) Subject
c) Effective date
d) Revised date
e) Number of pages
f) References
g) Rescinded directives
h) Amended directives

2. Elements of the body of the order include:
a) Policy Statement
b) Definition Statement (optional)
c) Procedures
d) Rules and Regulations (optional)
3. Orders will follow a standard outline form.
4. The order will end with the signature of the Superintendent.
B. All written directives in the Policy & Procedure manual shall be dated and indexed with
an identifying category. The first number of the sequence will correspond with the
category. The manual will contain eight categories, which will have a distinct identification
number. The following are the categories:
1. Chapter 1 Fire Service Role and Authority (100s)
2. Chapter 2 Organization and Administration (200s)
3. Chapter 3 General Operations (300s)
4. Chapter 4 Fire Prevention (400s)
5. Chapter 5 Emergency Medical Services (500s)
6. Chapter 6 Training (600s)
7. Chapter 7 Equipment and Technology (700s)
8. Chapter 8 Records Management (800s)
9. Chapter 9 Safety (900s)
10. Chapter 10 Personnel (1000s)
11. Chapter 11 Facility (1100s)
IV. DISCLAIMER
A. The provisions contained in the Policy Manual are not intended to create an employment
contract nor any employment rights or entitlements.
B. The policies contained within this manual are for the internal use of the Stickney Fire
Department and shall not be construed to create a higher standard or duty of care for
civil or criminal liability against the Village, its officials or members. Violations of any
provision of any policy contained within this manual shall only form the basis for
department administrative action, training or discipline.
C. The Stickney Fire Department reserves the right to revise any policy content, in whole or
in part at any time.
V. SEVERABILITY
A. In the event that any term or provision of this Policy Manual is declared illegal, invalid or
unenforceable by any court or any federal or state government agency, the remaining
terms and provisions that are not affected shall remain in full force and effect. If any
provision of the Policy Manual is found to be in conflict with a local, state or federal law,
Village policy or collective bargaining agreement, such law, Village policy or collective
bargaining agreement shall take precedence over that provision of the Policy Manual.

B. In the event that any of the terms or provisions of the Policy Manual are determined to
conflict with any portion of a collective bargaining agreement, the Department will seek
to resolve the conflict.
VI. DISTRIBUTION OF THE MANUAL
A. An electronic version of the Policy Manual will be made available to all members on the
Department network for viewing and printing. No changes shall be made to the manual
without authorization from the Fire Chief or the authorized designee.
B. Each member shall acknowledge that he/she has been provided access to, and has had
the opportunity to review, the Policy Manual and Interim directives. Members shall seek
clarification as needed from an appropriate supervisor for any provisions that they do not
fully understand.
VII. REVIEW AND REVISIONS OF THE POLICY MANUAL
A. The Fire Chief will ensure that the Policy Manual is periodically reviewed and updated as
necessary.
B. Directives should not conflict with established policies or procedures unless the order
constitutes a revision or replacement of an existing policy or procedure.
C. All revisions to the Policy Manual will be provided to each member on or before the date
the policy becomes effective. Each member will be required to acknowledge that he/she
has reviewed the revisions and shall seek clarification from an appropriate supervisor as
needed.
D. Members are responsible for keeping informed of all Policy Manual revisions.
E. Each Chief will ensure that members under his/her command are aware of any Policy
Manual revision.
F. All department members suggesting revision of the contents of the Policy Manual shall
forward their written suggestions to their supervisors, who will consider the
recommendations and forward them to the command staff as appropriate.
VIII. GENERAL ORDERS
A. General Orders will immediately modify or change and supersede the sections of this
Policy & Procedure manual to which they pertain.
B. The Fire Chief, or designee, shall issue all General Orders.
C. All department officers and/or supervisors shall be responsible for communicating
General Orders to all members under their command and/or direct supervision.
D. General Orders will be rescinded upon incorporation into this manual.
E. All General Orders shall be reviewed periodically to authenticate or determine if they are
currently applicable to the mission of the Department.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Mission, Philosophy And Goals
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to affirm the mission and philosophy of the department and provide
guidelines on the development of goals and objectives to achieve the mission.
POLICY:
The Stickney Fire Department is committed to maintaining the safety of the community with the highest
quality of service the department can provide. Supervisors will periodically review this statement of
philosophy and values with subordinates. The Stickney Fire Department will establish goals and objectives
for the Department and institute procedures for evaluating the progress made toward attaining these
goals and objectives.
I. MISSION
A. The mission of the Stickney Fire Department Is to safeguard the lives and property of the
Citizens of Stickney, by providing fire prevention and public education programs, effective
and efficient fire suppression, emergency medical, rescue and other emergency services.
B. The department will maintain, periodically review, and update the department mission
statement stating the department’s goals, values, and general philosophic approach to
safety.
II. GOALS AND OBJECTIVES
A. DEFINITIONS
1. Goals - Goals are a relatively broad statement of the end result that one intends
ultimately to achieve. A goal usually requires a relatively long timespan to achieve
and, whenever possible should be stated in a way that permits measurement of
its achievement.
2. Objectives - An objective is an end or a result that one intends to attain in order
to achieve partial fulfillment of a goal. An objective is a sub-goal or an element of
a goal, therefore, requires a shorter time to accomplish then does a goal.
B. PREPARATION
1. The Chief and Deputy Chief will establish written goals for the Stickney Fire
Department. The goals will be divided into two categories: Short-Term and Long-
Term.

2. These goals will be made available to all employees of the department to assist
in the setting of objectives.
3. Using the established goals, objectives will be established annually by each
organizational unit within the department as part of the department’s annual
budget process. Personnel representing all levels within the department will
participate in the annual process to define the objectives.
4. The objectives used to meet the goals will be forwarded through the chain of
command to the Deputy Chief who will consolidate and finalize the objectives and
forward the completed objectives to the Fire Chief.
C. The completed goals and objectives statement for the department will then be provided
to each employee.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Performance Of Duties
body:
PURPOSE:
This policy establishes daily performance expectations.
POLICY:
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to provide safe and appropriate responses to emergency
calls and for its members to provide professional and competent services.
In order to promote driver safety, it is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department that all members driving
department vehicles or equipment or driving a privately owned vehicle while conducting department
business, will have and maintain a valid driver's license on their person.
I. RESPONSIBILITIES
A. All members shall be familiar with, and in compliance with, the policies, standard
operating procedures, duties as assigned, and any other lawful instruction or order from
a superior officer.
B. All members, upon receipt of any emergency alarm, shall immediately cease all activities
and without delay report to their assigned apparatus, respond immediately to the fire or
other emergency dispatched, and exert reasonable effort to perform to the best of their
ability, given the totality of circumstances.
C. All members will exercise reasonable precautionary measures and good judgment to
avoid injury to themselves or others while on-duty. Members who witness or are made
aware of unsafe behavior should take appropriate steps to report or prevent such actions.
D. Members shall furnish their names and department identification numbers to any person
requesting that information, other than in situations in which the member’s personal
safety is at risk.
II. COMPETENT PERFORMANCE
A. Members should perform their duties in a manner which will maintain the highest
standards of efficiency in carrying out the functions and objectives of the Department.
Unsatisfactory performance may include, but not be limited to, the following:
1. Excessive or unauthorized leave
2. Tardiness
3. Demonstration of a lack of knowledge

4. Failure to conform to the work standards established for the member’s position
5. Any other failure to demonstrate good conduct
6. Insubordination
7. Noncompliance with department policy, guidelines, rules, directives and orders
B. All members shall complete and submit all necessary reports, forms and memos on time
and in accordance with any other applicable department policy or procedure. Reports,
forms and memos submitted by members shall be truthful and complete. No member
shall knowingly enter or cause to be entered any inaccurate, incomplete, false or
improper information.
C. Members shall report to the Fire Chief, or his designee, the loss or recovery of any
department badge, identification card, key, or equipment. In the case of an equipment
loss, a police report should be filed in the jurisdiction where the loss occurred.
III. DRIVER'S LICENSE
A. All members shall possess a valid state-issued driver's license and the appropriate training
required for their assigned duties as approved by the Fire Chief or the authorized
designee.
B. All members shall be familiar with the state vehicle code, any manuals specific to driving
or operating department apparatus and all other applicable department policies and
procedures.
C. All members shall report to the Fire Chief, or his designee, any change in their driver's
license’s status. Failure to maintain a valid driver's license in accordance with an
employee’s current classification specification may result in disciplinary action.
D. REVIEW OF RECORDS
1. The Fire Chief shall appoint an officer to monitor the driving records of all
members who are assigned duties that require driving while conducting
department business, to confirm each driver has a valid driver's license and to
monitor driver records for potential problem behavior.
2. The officer appointed to monitor driving records shall be responsible for
reviewing the driver's license reports as part of the hiring process and any time
an incident occurs that affects a member’s eligibility to drive.
3. Whenever the officer appointed to monitor driving records becomes aware of
changes that could affect a member’s eligibility to drive, the officer should notify
the affected member and the member’s immediate supervisor
E. NEW EMPLOYEES
1. Prospective member driving records shall be evaluated to confirm that the
applicant has a valid driver's license and to review the type and number of traffic
violations and accidents on the record.
2. At the time of hire, a new members shall be required to present a valid driver's
license.

F. CURRENT EMPLOYEES
1. Any member must immediately notify his/her supervisor of any suspension,
revocation or other change in the status of his/her driver's license. Any violation
of this procedure may result in disciplinary action, up to and including
termination.
2. If a member’s driver's license is suspended, revoked or becomes invalid, the
Department may, at its discretion, take any combination of the following actions:
a) May allow the member, for up to 60 days, an opportunity to seek the
reinstatement of his/her driver's license, provided:
(1) The member can still perform the majority of his/her job duties.
(2) There is minimal impact on the Department work output.
b) Place a member on leave without pay for up to a maximum of six months
from the date of the issuing entity report pending license reinstatement.
c) Any member who is unable to obtain reinstatement of his/her driver's
license may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including
termination.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Conduct And Behavior
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide guidelines to prevent activities or behaviors that may lead to
disciplinary actions or possible dismissal.
POLICY:
It is the policy of this department that its members strive to attain the highest professional standard of
conduct and discharge their duties in a courteous and professional manner. New employees will be
instructed in the Rules of Conduct.
I. PROFESSIONAL CONDUCT
A. All members shall be governed by the ordinary and reasonable rules of behavior observed
by law-abiding and self-respecting citizens and should conduct themselves at all times in
such manner as to reflect favorably on the Department. Conduct unbecoming of a
member shall include that which discredits the Department or the person as a member
of the Department or which impairs the operation or efficiency of the Department or its
members.
B. All members shall conduct themselves in a manner that will not impair the good order
and discipline of the Department. Members shall not, while on-duty, indulge in offensive,
obscene or uncivil language, verbal or physical altercations or threats thereof, or conduct
which might cause injury to another person.
C. All members of the Department shall be familiar with the expected standard of behavior,
both on- and off-duty.
II. RESPONSIBILITIES OF ALL EMPLOYEES
A. The code of ethics (Policy 101) will be regarded as guiding principles for daily ethical living.
B. INTERACTION WITH THE PUBLIC
In the performance of their duties, members shall be courteous to the public and tactful.
They should control their tempers, should exercise reasonable patience and discretion,
and should not engage in any argumentative discussions even when provoked.
In the performance of their duties, members shall not use coarse, violent, profane, or
insolent language or gestures, and should not express prejudice or discrimination.

C. COURTESY TO MEMBERS
Members shall be courteous and respectful in their relations with all members of the
Department. Members shall not use coarse, violent, profane, or insolent language or
gestures, and shall not express prejudice or discrimination.
D. CONFORMANCE TO LAWS
Members shall obey all laws of the United States and of any state and local jurisdiction in
which the member is present.
E. DEROGATORY OR MALICIOUS STATEMENTS
Members shall not be a party to any malicious gossip, report or activity which would tend
to disrupt department morale or bring discredit to the Department or any member
thereof. Member questions concerning department policy, activities, officers and/or
safety issues shall be submitted by official written communication to the member’s
immediate supervisor.
F. POLITICAL ACTIVITY
Members shall not engage in political activities of any kind while on-duty. Members are
also prohibited from engaging in any political activity off-duty while wearing any uniform
items or equipment that could identify them as members of the Department.
G. SEXUAL ACTIVITY
Members shall not engage in any sexual activity while on-duty. This includes use of any
electronic device to communicate or receive messages, photos or any other content of a
sexual or provocative nature.
H. ILLEGAL GAMBLING
Members shall not engage or participate in any form of illegal gambling at any time while
on- duty. This includes accessing gaming websites from computers or any electronic
device, whether department-issued or owned by the member.
I. GIFTS AND GRATUITIES
Members shall not solicit or accept any gift, including money, tangible or intangible
personal property, or any service, gratuity, favor, entertainment, hospitality, loan,
promise, or any other thing of value from any person, business or organization that is
doing business with, or seeking to do business with, the Department or the Village.
If it may reasonably be inferred that the person, business, or organization seeks to
influence the actions of a member or seeks to affect the performance of a member while
on-duty, the incident should be immediately reported to the next level supervisor.
J. OFFERS OF DONATIONS AND GIFTS OF THE HEART
Members who are approached with monetary donations following major disasters shall
direct the person or entity to the Administration Division for instruction on proper ways
to donate.
At no time shall a member accept any monetary donation from the public. If a citizen
offers a gift of a non-monetary nature, such as food or product, the gift shall be placed in
an area of the station or office to be shared by all members. At no time shall a member
consider a gift of the heart as a personal present.

K. ABUSE OF POSITION
Members shall not use their official positions, official identification cards, or badges to
avoid the consequences of illegal acts or for other non-work-related personal gain.
Members shall not lend to another person their identification cards or badges or permit
their identification cards or badges to be photographed or reproduced without the
approval of the Fire Chief.
Members shall not authorize the use of their names, photographs, or official titles that
identify them as department members (e.g., in connection with testimonials or
advertisements of any commodity or commercial enterprise) without the approval of the
Fire Chief.
L. PUBLIC STATEMENTS AND APPEARANCES
Members shall not address public gatherings, appear on radio or television, prepare any
articles for publication, act as correspondents to a newspaper or periodical, or release or
divulge investigative information or information on any other matter of the Department
while presenting themselves or in any way identifying themselves as representing the
Department, without the approval of the Fire Chief or his designee.
M. DISCRIMINATION, OPPRESSION, OR FAVORITISM
Unless required by law or policy, discriminating against, oppressing, or providing
favoritism to any person because of actual or perceived characteristics such as race,
ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression,
age, disability, economic status, cultural group, veteran status, marital status, and any
other classification or status protected by law, or intentionally denying or impeding
another in the exercise or enjoyment of any right, privilege, power, or immunity, knowing
the conduct is unlawful, is prohibited.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Emergency Action Plan And Fire Prevention Plan
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide for member and visitor safety in the event of an emergency at any
department facility and ensure compliance with the Illinois Health and Safety Act and the Code of Federal
Regulations mandating all employers to develop and maintain an Emergency Action Plan (EAP) and a Fire
Prevention Plan (FPP) (820 ILCS 219/25; 29 CFR 1910.38; 29 CFR 1910.39).
POLICY:
The Stickney Fire Department is committed to preparing for natural or human-created emergency
incidents and providing for the safety of its members and visitors. It is the policy of the Stickney Fire
Department to provide training to all members regarding the EAP and FPP.
I. EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN (EAP) AND FIRE PREVENTION PLAN (FPP)
A. The Fire Chief or his designee will develop and maintain an EAP and FPP to provide for the
safety of department members and visitors in the event of an emergency. The EAP and
FPP will address the specific requirements contained in 29 CFR 1910.38 and 29 CFR
1910.39 and will address all buildings, facilities and regular places of work or visitor access
that are controlled by the Department. The plan also will address actions that members
of the Department must take to ensure their safety and that of visitors from fire and other
emergencies.
B. The EAP shall be in writing and its elements shall include, but are not limited to (29 CFR
1910.38):
1. Emergency evacuation procedures including escape procedures and emergency
escape route assignments.
2. Procedures to be followed by members who remain to conduct critical facility
operations before they evacuate.
3. Procedures to account for all members and visitors after an emergency
evacuation has been completed.
4. Rescue and medical duties.
5. Means of reporting fires and other emergencies.
6. Names and job titles of persons or departments that can be contacted for further
information or an explanation of duties under the plan.

7. The alarm system that will be used to notify members and visitors in the event of
a fire or other emergency situation.
8. The types of evacuations to be used in emergency circumstances.
C. The FPP shall be in writing and its elements shall include, but are not limited to (29 CFR
1910.39):
1. A list of major fire hazards, handling and storage procedures for hazardous
materials, potential ignition sources and their control procedures and the type of
fire equipment necessary to control the hazard.
2. Names and job titles of persons responsible for maintaining the equipment to
prevent or control sources of ignition or fires.
3. Names and job titles of persons responsible for control of fuel source hazards.
4. Procedures to control the accumulation of flammable and combustible waste.
5. Maintenance procedures for heat-producing equipment to prevent accidental
ignition of combustible materials.
D. The written EAP and FPP shall be kept at each department workplace or facility and shall
be made available for member and visitor review.
II. EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN AND FIRE PREVENTION PLAN TRAINING
A. The EAP and FPP training shall include, but is not limited to:
1. A review of the department’s EAP and FPP including any information specific to
each member’s workplace or assignment.
2. Information on where written copies of the EAP and FPP are located and how
members may review the plans.
3. The Department shall designate and train a sufficient number of people to assist
in the safe and orderly emergency evacuation of members and visitors in the
event of an emergency.
4. The Department shall advise each member of his/her responsibility under the
plans at the following times:
a) Initially when the plans are developed
b) Whenever the member's responsibilities or designated actions under the
plans change
c) Whenever the plans are changed
5. The Department shall review with each member upon initial assignment those
parts of the EAP and FPP that the member must know to protect the member in
the event of an emergency.
B. The Training Officer shall be responsible for developing and scheduling the department’s
EAP and FPP training. The Training Officer shall maintain records of all EAP and FPP
training provided to members. Records should include, but are not limited to:
1. The dates of the training sessions.

2. A list of the topics or a summary of the content of the training sessions.
3. The names or other identifiers and job titles of the members who received the
training.
4. The names, certificate numbers and qualifications of persons conducting the
training.
C. The Training Officer should maintain the training records in accordance with established
records retention schedules.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Disclosure Of Economic Interests
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide a uniform method for complying with state law requirements for
filing a statement of economic interests by designated members (5 ILCS 420/4A-101.5 et seq.).
POLICY:
Designated members shall comply with state requirements for filing a statement of economic interests
with the Village. (Illinois Governmental Ethics Act)
I. DEPARTMENT RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The Fire Chief shall designate a person to be the conflict-of-interest filing officer for the
Department, who shall be responsible for administering the filings, including ensuring
timely compliance with the Village and maintaining a list of all department members who
are required to file a statement (5 ILCS 420/4A-106.5).
B. All such statements shall be screened for compliance and potential conflicts of interest by
the conflict-of-interest filing officer. Members in designated classifications are required
to disclose certain economic interests, which may include investments, interests in real
property, as well as income and business interests (5 ILCS 420/4A-102).
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Liability Claims
body:
PURPOSE:
This policy provides guidelines for the management of all claims, including personal injury and property
loss or damage, filed against the Department.
POLICY:
It is the policy of this department to evaluate and resolve claims in a timely manner, as appropriate.
I. RESPONSIBILITY
A. The Fire Chief will designate a risk management team to receive, investigate and evaluate
any claim for loss or damage received by the Department.
B. Any member of this department who becomes aware of any potential for a claim or
lawsuit, or who receives a formal written claim against the Department, shall forward the
information to the risk management team as soon as practicable.
II. RESPONSE TO CLAIMS
A. The risk management team will investigate all claims for money or damages received and
will resolve claims as appropriate and within guidelines approved by the Fire Chief and
the department’s governing body.
B. The risk manager shall ensure the claim is accepted or rejected. Notice of acceptance or
rejection shall be given to the claimant in writing and in compliance with state law. If a
claim is rejected because it was filed late, the notice shall state that the claim was
returned as untimely.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Department Communications
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish guidelines, format, and authority levels for the various types of
administrative communication documents in existence within the Department. This policy will establish
guidelines for the proper use and application of the various communications methods provided by the
Department.
POLICY:
The Stickney Fire Department encourages and supports the exchange of information among all agency
functions and personnel for the purpose of coordinating activities. There are a number of ways to
communicate information, such as attendance at staff meetings, e-mail, voice mail, other electronic
systems, and exchange of daily bulletins.
It shall be the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to control the use of the name, logo, and image of
the Department as well as the use of letterhead, to ensure that official administrative communications
representing the Stickney Fire Department follow a specific format and are released only by persons with
the authority to do so.
I. GENERAL COMMUNICATION
A. Communication, coordination and cooperation among agency personnel and functions is
essential to maintaining a high level of service to the public.
B. Information may be relayed through a variety of ways, including meetings, using the
Village’s email system, memorandums, patrol notices, or any other written or oral means
to exchange information.
C. Information may also be relayed by posting on the bulletin board with the approval of a
supervisor.
D. All personnel provide a vital role in agency development and personnel training; policy
and procedural development and implementation; and improving inter-departmental
communications.
II. DIRECTIVES AND ORDERS
A. Members shall comply with lawful directives and orders from any department supervisor
or person in a position of authority, absent a reasonable and bona fide justification.

B. A member who believes any written or verbal order to be unlawful or in conflict with
another order shall:
1. Immediately inform the supervisor issuing the order, and also the member's
immediate supervisor or the Fire Chief of the conflict or error of the order.
2. Provide details explaining the grounds for believing there is a conflict or error.
3. Request clarification, guidance and direction regarding following the order.
4. Request the order in writing, absent exigent circumstances, should the conflict or
perceived error be unresolved.
5. Respectfully inform the supervisor that he/she intends to disobey what he/she
reasonably believes to be a conflicting or unlawful order.
C. A member's decision to disobey an order that he/she believes to be unlawful is not a bar
to discipline should the order be determined as lawful.
III. CORRESPONDENCE
A. Outgoing Correspondence
1. In order to ensure that the letterhead and name of the Department are not
misused, all external correspondence shall be on department letterhead.
2. Members may not send correspondence representing the Stickney Fire
Department to outside agencies without the authorization of the Fire Chief or his
designee.
3. All department letterhead shall bear the signature element of the Fire Chief in
addition to the actual signature of an authorized signer. Members of the
Department may use letterhead only for official business and with approval of
their supervisor.
B. Incoming Correspondence
1. All incoming correspondence will be routed to the office of the Fire Chief.
2. No person shall open department correspondence other than the Fire Chief,
designated Administrative Staff or other person designated by the Fire Chief.
3. Department personnel should discourage friends and/or relatives, businesses,
etc. from sending non-police related correspondence to the Village or Fire
Department for them. Department members shall not use the department
address for private purposes without the permission of the Fire Chief.
4. Correspondence received by the Fire Chief or individual Divisions shall be
stamped with the appropriate date received stamp.
5. All incoming subpoenas and court notices will be forwarded to Records for
processing and distribution to the appropriate Department employee.
IV. MEMORANDUMS
A. Memorandums are a necessary and important component of effective operations at all
levels of the Department. For the purposes of efficiency and to ensure appropriate
distribution of written communications, memorandums between department members
may be distributed via email.

B. Memorandums typically are used to memorialize and/or summarize communication and
facts. Memorandums can be generated by a supervisor and sent to subordinates or a
group of subordinates to give direction, clarify a policy decision or request an action by
another division. A memorandum also may be written by line-level members to
communicate information. If the recipient is of higher rank than the member’s immediate
supervisor or is outside the Department, the information should be approved by the
proper chain of command before being forwarded to the recipient.
C. Recommendations for a standardized department memorandum shall include the
following within the body of the written text or email:
1. A standard heading, including the name of the Department.
2. The date of the memorandum.
3. The intended recipient of the memorandum.
4. The name, rank and division of the department member creating the
memorandum.
5. A brief statement of the subject of the memorandum.
V. SURVEYS
A. All surveys made in the name of the Department shall be authorized by the Fire Chief or
his designee.
B. A copy of the completed survey will be emailed to the Fire Chief.
VI. DEPARTMENT FLYERS, POSTINGS, AND HANDOUTS
A. All flyers, postings, or handouts bearing the name, likeness, or containing information
pertaining to the Stickney Fire Department shall be approved by the Fire Chief, or his
designee, prior to dissemination.
B. This will apply to any flyers, postings, or handouts that are both internal and external.
C. Failure to obtain approval before the dissemination of the above defined communications
from the Fire Chief, or his designee, will result in discipline, up to and including
termination.
VII. PERSONNEL ORDERS
A. Personnel orders may be issued periodically by the Fire Chief, or his designee to announce
and document promotions, hiring of new personnel, separations, personnel and group
commendations, or other changes in status.
VIII. COMMAND STAFF MEETINGS
A. The Stickney Fire Department will conduct regular staff meetings in order to maintain an
effective communication network.
B. These meetings are held as authorized by the Fire Chief.
1. Periodic Command briefings will be held when called by the Chief. The purpose
of these meetings is to provide information on department-wide activities and
programs to supervisors, managers, and commanders. An agenda will be
prepared, and minutes kept.

2. Division staff meetings are called at the direction of the individual Deputy Chief
and may or may not include all division supervisors and/or division employees.
3. Supervisors may call such other meetings of all their personnel as may be
required to ensure effective and efficient management.
IX. ALTERNATE CHANNELS OF COMMUNICATION
A. All members shall endeavor to keep their supervisors informed of any matters that may
affect the safety, welfare or operations of the Department.
B. As a general matter, any concern about a workplace situation should first be raised with
the member’s immediate supervisor. It is recognized, however, that there may be
occasions where the use of the established chain of command may not be appropriate. If
an issue is of a personal nature, involves a sensitive matter, is of significant importance to
the Department or involves other members or supervisors, the member may consult
directly with the Chief, the Fire Chief or a representative of the Administration.
C. All members are free to make or prepare to make, in good faith, any complaint that
identifies ethical or legal violations, including fraud, waste, abuse of authority, gross
mismanagement, violations of the law or practices that may pose a threat to the health,
safety and security of the public or members without fear of actual or threatened
discrimination, retaliation or reprisal. Such complaints are not subject to the chain of
command and may be made to any supervisor, the Administration or any government law
enforcement agency (740 ILCS 174/10). Nothing in this policy shall diminish the rights or
remedies of a member pursuant to any applicable federal law, provision of the U.S.
Constitution, applicable state law, ordinance or collective bargaining agreement.
D. Any form of reprisal or retaliation against any member for making or filing a complaint in
good faith or for participating in the investigation of a complaint is prohibited. Any
member engaging in any form or type of reprisal or retaliation is subject to discipline.
X. ELECTRONIC MAIL
A. PRIVACY EXPECTATION
1. Members forfeit any expectation of privacy with regard to emails or anything
published, shared, transmitted or maintained through file-sharing software or
any Internet site that is accessed, transmitted, received or reviewed on any
department technology system.
2. The Department reserves the right to access, audit and disclose, for whatever
reason, any message, including attachments, and any information accessed,
transmitted, received or reviewed over any technology that is issued or
maintained by the Department, including the Department email system,
computer network or any information placed into storage on any department
system or device. The fact that access to a database, service or website requires
a username or password will not create an expectation of privacy if it is accessed
through department computers, electronic devices, or networks.

B. RESTRICTED USE
1. Messages transmitted over the email system are restricted to official business
activities or shall only contain information that is essential for the
accomplishment of business-related tasks or for communications that are directly
related to the business, administration, or practices of the Department.
2. Sending derogatory, defamatory, obscene, disrespectful, sexually suggestive,
harassing or any other inappropriate messages on the email system is prohibited
and will result in discipline.
3. Email messages addressed to the entire department are only to be used for
official business-related items that are of particular interest to all users. In the
event that a member has questions about sending a particular email
communication, the member should seek prior approval from his/ her supervisor.
4. It is a violation of this policy to transmit a message under another member’s name
or email address or to use the password of another to log into the system unless
directed to do so by a supervisor. Members are required to log off the network
or secure the workstation when the computer is unattended. This added security
measure will minimize the potential misuse of a member’s email, name or
password.
C. EMAIL RECORD MANAGEMENT
1. Email may, depending upon the individual content, be a public record under the
Illinois Freedom of Information Act and must be managed in accordance with the
established records retention schedule and in compliance with state law (5 ILCS
140/1.1 et seq.).
2. The Freedom of Information Officer (5 ILCS 140/3.5) shall ensure that email
messages are retained and recoverable as outlined in the Records Management
Policy.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Post-Incident Analysis (PIA)
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish a uniform Post-Incident Analysis (PIA) to identify strengths and
weakness within the Department. This policy describes the various types of PIA that can be used in the
evaluation of department performance. A PIA may also be used to identify equipment needs and training
needs. The information collected during the PIA process also may be useful in justifying future funding
requests for equipment, personnel and/or training.
POLICY:
The PIA is a valuable tool to improve the overall operations of the fire service. It is the policy of this
department to use the PIA as a tool for Incident Commanders (IC), Officers in Charges, and command staff
to identify areas of strength and weakness within the Department on an incident- by-incident basis, for
the purpose of continuous improvement.
The PIA may additionally be utilized in department-wide training to communicate continuous
improvement of emergency scene operations and fireground safety.
I. RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The IC, Officer in Charge, and command staff have shared responsibility for the overall
effectiveness of the PIA process.
B. The IC should informally analyze every incident to improve personnel, unit and system
performance. After every major incident or special event, the IC should develop a PIA to
determine strengths, weaknesses and lessons learned about the incident operation.
C. Anyone may request a PIA of a particular incident. Any PIA requests must be made
through the chain of command.
D. Any significant safety issue that is identified in the PIA should be addressed immediately,
if it was not already resolved prior to the PIA being completed. If appropriate, a report
should be sent to the International Association of Fire Chiefs (IAFC) Near-Miss Reporting
System on any significant safety issues.
II. POST-INCIDENT ANALYSIS
A. A PIA should be completed within 30 days of an incident and may result in
recommendations for changes to procedures, equipment use, policy and/or training to
better enable the Department to serve the community.

B. A PIA should include lessons learned from the observation of effective and efficient
methods of mitigating a major incident. These include all strategic decisions, operational
issues, built-in fire protection devices and anything else that assisted in mitigating the
incident.
C. A PIA may include:
1. Evaluation of the overall operational effectiveness.
2. Evaluation of safety procedures.
3. Evaluation of the success or failure of tactical objectives.
4. Evaluation of the application and effectiveness of policies and/or procedures.
5. Specific knowledge that might be beneficial.
D. The information gained from a PIA should be used by the Stickney Fire Department to:
1. Reinforce the incident management system.
2. Evaluate current training programs and/or identify training needs.
3. Evaluate current policies and procedures.
4. Identify and prioritize planning needs for the future.
5. Identify equipment problems/concerns.
6. Evaluate fire prevention inspection and public education effectiveness.
III. TYPES OF POST-INCIDENT ANALYSIS
A. HOT WASH
1. An incident “hot wash” should be performed at the incident scene prior to the
release of equipment or personnel. A hot wash is a meeting of all involved
personnel on-scene. It is an informal briefing of the incident, the actions taken,
and problems encountered. An IC may present an analysis with key companies or
crews while they are on-scene. The advantage to this is that crews are present,
and all aspects of the call are still fresh. One disadvantage to a hot wash might
occur at medical incidents, when some members may be caring for patients and
are unable to participate.
2. If the analysis takes place while on-scene, it is the responsibility of the IC to:
a) Meet in a safe area, even if it requires relocating to another area.
b) Consider the impact of company downtime.
c) Consider public perception.
B. INFORMAL PIA
1. An informal PIA is used following smaller multi-company incidents, such as
structure fires, medical incidents or special operations incidents.
2. The IC or a designated representative should arrange for and conduct the
informal analysis.

C. COMPANY-LEVEL PIA
1. A company-level PIA is highly encouraged and should be a standard
communication tool for all Company Officers. It is appropriate for significant
incidents involving single companies as well as multiple-company stations where
more than one company participated in the incident.
2. Company-level analysis promotes unity and teamwork, enhances
communication, improves company performance and is a useful tool for
evaluating the health and welfare of crew members following certain traumatic
incidents. A company-level PIA can take place while at the fire station or any
location that provides privacy. A company level PIA does not take the place of,
nor negate the need for Critical Incident Stress Debriefing, (CISD) when
appropriate.
D. FORMAL PIA
1. A formal PIA should be conducted following all:
a) Multiple-alarm structure fires.
b) Multiple-alarm brush fires.
c) Multiple-alarm Emergency Medical Service (EMS) incidents.
d) Multiple-alarm special operations incidents.
e) Major disaster drills.
f) Any unusual incident identified by the IC or other officers.
2. A formal PIA should be considered for:
a) A building fire in which three or more rooms are severely damaged by
fire, or where unusual extinguishment problems existed.
b) Any incident in which an unusual event occurs (e.g., explosion, collapse).
c) Any fire resulting in a fatality.
d) Any fire resulting in injury to firefighters that is serious enough to require
transport to a medical facility.
e) Any “close call” incident where firefighters could have been injured.
f) Any hazardous materials incident with multi-company involvement.
g) Any specialty rescue operation with multi-company involvement.
h) Any incident, at the IC’s discretion or at the request of a Company Officer.
3. The Training Chief is responsible for scheduling and facilitating the presentation
of all formal PIAs. This will include:
a) Setting a presentation date and location within three days (whenever
possible) of the incident.

b) Supervising the completion of an incident analysis packet that should
include a summary of the incident, drawings and identification of any
lessons learned.
c) Developing a written After Action Report (AAR) summarizing the PIA and
submitting it to the Fire Chief for approval and distribution.
d) Notifying of Shift Commanders.
e) Coordinating/scheduling with other departments or outside agencies
that worked the incident.
f) Arranging move-up and/or cover companies from other departments.
4. The Fire Chief, or his designee, is responsible for notifications to all members of
the shift who are scheduled to attend the PIA. All members should be notified
within one week if a formal PIA is being arranged to allow them to prepare or
gather any necessary documentation.
5. Copies of the AAR should be posted at each fire station for all personnel to review.
E. A copy of all PIAs and AARs shall be forwarded to the Fire Chief, or his designee, for
approval prior to distribution, including any determinations or conclusions reached
through the PIA presentations.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Annual Planning Master Calendar
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to ensure the development of a master schedule of annual activities that will
assist with the overall planning and coordination of department resources, training, and other activities.
POLICY:
The Stickney Fire Department will establish, update, and maintain a master schedule of annual activities
to facilitate the overall planning and coordination of activities and resources. The calendar of training
events will be released and posted on an every-other-month basis.
I. DEFINITIONS
A. Target hazard - A building or occupancy that is unusually dangerous in terms of life loss,
or that has a high potential for property damage. A target hazard is often the subject of a
target hazard assessment and training by virtue of its potential to overload equipment
and personnel resources; involve atypical hazards; require special technical advice;
require a multi-agency response; involve complex firefighting operations; or have a
significant impact on the community if the building or occupancy were destroyed.
II. RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The Chief officers in charge of Training, Fire Prevention, Maintenance, and EMS are
responsible for creating and maintaining a calendar that includes a schedule of all training
required in compliance with state and federal regulations, required inspections and other
significant activities.
B. The calendar should include at a minimum:
1. All necessary National Incident Management System (NIMS) and Illinois
Department of Labor (IDOL) training.
2. All department emergency medical members (EMR, EMT, EMT-I, A-EMT and EMT-
P) relicensure training as necessary to meet the requirements of the local
Emergency Medical Service (EMS) authority and the Illinois Department of Public
Health Division of Emergency Medical Systems and Highway Safety, or the
National Registry.
3. Training required for maintaining competencies in job-specific duties and
functions, including emergency response roles, the Incident Command System
(ICS) and approved Illinois Office of the State Fire Marshal Division of Personnel

Standards and Education (OSFM-PSE) courses, in addition to hazardous material
training, wildland interface training and target hazard training as required by
federal, state and local law or regulatory agency. Training may include
manipulative exercises, didactic classroom work and simulations.
4. An inspection and review of all plot plans and pre-fire plans.
5. Protective clothing inspections.
6. Self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) inspections and testing.
7. Hose and ladder inspection, including aerial inspections.
8. Vehicle and pump capacity inspection and testing.
9. Annual medical evaluation of personnel.
10. Annual quantitative and qualitative fit testing of respiratory protection devices.
11. All other training and inspections required by any federal, Illinois or local agency
requirement.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Solicitation Of Funds
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to ensure that fundraising activities associated with the Department are
consistent with its mission, values and legal status. This policy applies to all fundraising activities involving
the Department or the use of the department name, insignias, equipment or facilities.
POLICY:
It shall be the policy of this department that all fundraising activities involving the name, logo, or image
of the Stickney Fire Department, on-duty members, or use of department equipment for the financial
benefit of the Department, must be authorized by the Fire Chief or his designee prior to initiating
solicitations. The Fire Chief or his authorized designee may prohibit the use of the Stickney Fire
Department name, logo, or image for any fundraising activities deemed to be inconsistent with the
mission of the Stickney Fire Department or detrimental to the image of the Stickney Fire Department.
Authorized fundraising activities should not indicate or imply that a donation will influence services
provided by the Department. Members engaged in fundraising activities are expected to act ethically
regarding the solicitation of funds, the interaction with donors or potential donors and the maintenance
of fundraising records.
I. DEFINITIONS
A. Fundraising - The collection of money through donations, sales or event programming for
the purpose of charitable donation or organizational budget enhancement.
II. GUIDELINES
A. Fundraising activities or events involving the Department should incorporate the
following elements:
1. Compliance with applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations.
2. Compliance with department and governing-body policies.
3. A benefit to the Department that is consistent with the department mission.
4. An accurate description of the purpose for which funds are requested.
5. A limitation on the frequency of solicitations to avoid placing undue pressure on
donors.

6. Identification of the individual soliciting funds as a volunteer, a member of this
department or a hired solicitor.
7. An admonishment that encourages donors to seek independent advice if there is
reason to believe that a proposed gift might significantly affect the donor’s
financial position, taxable income or relationship with other family members.
8. The assurance that donor requests to limit the frequency of contacts, to prohibit
solicitation by telephone or other technology and to reduce or cease sending
printed or electronically transmitted material concerning the Department will be
honored.
9. Respect of donors’ privacy and a commitment that the Department will not sell
donors’ names and contact information.
B. Commercial or corporate sponsorship of fundraising activities or events may be allowed
provided that it has been preapproved by the Fire Chief or his/her designee.
III. DEPARTMENT-SPONSORED EVENTS
A. The following also apply to department-sponsored fundraising events:
1. Fundraising events should be clearly identified by a sign indicating the name,
product, service, price and purpose of the event.
2. At least one member should be present during the entire event.
3. Individuals participating in the event should be briefed and supervised to ensure
their activities are consistent with this policy.
4. Individuals participating in the event should not be compensated by a
commission or a percentage of the amount collected.
5. Funds raised should be deposited no later than the next business day.
6. All donors should receive a receipt for the amount of their donation. In efforts
involving a less formal “drop” collection, receipts need not be issued unless
requested.
7. Fundraising activities should not delay emergency response or otherwise
compromise the mission of the organization.
8. Fundraising that takes place on public-owned or private property will be done
with the knowledge and approval of the property custodian or owner.
IV. FUNDRAISING ON BEHALF OF OTHERS
A. Fundraising for the benefit of a nonprofit charitable third party (e.g., blood drive, burn
victims, surviving families) having no direct affiliation with the Department is permissible
provided that the fundraising standards and event prerequisites listed above are
followed.
B. Any materials associated with a third-party fundraising activity shall be approved by the
Fire Chief or his designee prior to the activity. In addition, there should be a written
agreement between the Department and the organizers of the activity that includes:
1. Written verification that the event is for a charitable purpose.

2. Assignment of responsibility to the organizers for all direct costs incurred for the
event.
3. Assignment of responsibility to the organizers for the collection and reporting of
any applicable taxes.
4. Written instructions regarding the maintenance of funds raised on behalf of
others. The funds shall be maintained in a separate fund and not commingled
with other department funds.
C. The Department reserves the right to require additional conditions including, but not
limited to, evidence of insurance coverage or appropriate indemnification.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Village Of Stickney Risk Management Plan
body:
PURPOSE:
Risk management is the process of reducing the Village's exposure to claims and legal actions that are the
result of unsafe conditions or improper actions. Risk management includes maintaining a safe workplace,
avoiding accidents and injuries, fitness for duty, assuring that public properties and rights-of-way are in
proper condition, reporting unsafe conditions and transferring risk in contractual agreements when
appropriate. To work effectively, risk management must be an integral part of the operations of all
departments and the personal responsibility of each employee.
POLICY:
The Policy is a guide to help employees and public officials understand the major components of the risk
management process. The complete Risk Management Plan is in Appendix A.
I. RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN COMPONENTS
A. Accident Reporting
B. Claims Analysis
C. Unsafe Conditions
D. General Liability
E. Contractual Risk Management
F. Health/Disease Prevention
II. EXECUTIVE SAFETY COMMITTEE
A. The Executive Safety Committee is an integral part of the Village of Stickney overall risk
management plan. This is one place where management and employees can truly come
together as one to create results.
B. To be effective, the committee must interact in an environment of open communication
and have a desire to make a difference. By defining their goals and objectives, the
committee can create a shared vision that will enable action and promote a safe work
environment for all employees.
C. The Executive Safety Committee is made up of the following members:
1. One Village Trustee
2. Three members of Administration

3. Two members of Police Department
4. Two members of Public Works
5. Three members of Fire Department
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief
Appendix A - Risk Management Plan

SFD 209 – VILLAGE OF STICKNEY RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN Appendix A
VILLAGE OF STICKNEY RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN
A Guide for Employees, Department Heads and Public Officials
I. INTRODUCTION
Risk management is the process of reducing the Village's exposure
to claims and legal actions that are the result of unsafe conditions
or improper actions. Risk management includes maintaining a safe
workplace, avoiding accidents and injuries, fitness for duty, assuring
that public properties and rights-of-way are in proper condition,
reporting unsafe conditions and transferring risk in contractual
agreements when appropriate. To work effectively, risk
management must be an integral part of the operations of all
departments and the personal responsibility of each employee.
The Policy is a guide to help employees and public officials
understand the major components of the risk management process.
II. RISK MANAGER
The Chairperson of the Village Board Insurance and Safety
Committee, as authorized by the corporate authorities, directs the
Risk Management Program for the Member. Specific
responsibilities include:
A. To establish the objectives of the Risk Management Program
for the Member.
B. To appoint a Safety Coordinator who is responsible for the
organization, coordination and implementation of safety
related programs.
C. To develop in Department Heads a strong commitment to
support the Member's risk management objectives and a
clear understanding of their respective safety related duties
and responsibilities.
D. To chair the Executive Safety Committee Meetings and to
guide the Committee toward achieving the goals set forth in
the Risk Management Program. To publish and disseminate
an agenda for each meeting and to collect and distribute
other materials necessary for the discussion of agenda
items.
E. To review the annual Rick Management Program audits and
to appraise the effectiveness of the Program.

III. SAFETY COORDINATOR
The Safety Coordinator is responsible for organizing, coordinating
and implementing the Member's safety-related programs and
education.
Specific responsibilities include:
A. To advise the Risk Manager, Department Heads and
Supervisory Personnel on accident prevention by
recommending action designed to correct problem areas.
B. As a member of the Executive Safety Committee, will chair
meetings in the absence of the Risk Manager and perform
his duties.
C. To act as liaison between the Executive Safety Committee
and the Employee Safety Committee and to serve as advisor
to the members of the Employee Safety Committee.
D. To secure the assistance of Department Heads, Supervisors,
State and IRMA Officials as is necessary to effectuate the
Member's Risk Management Program and to inform the
Executive Safety Committee about the status of matters
affecting the Program.
E. To review departmentally generated Self-Inspection Reports
and to take appropriate action to correct the problems
revealed by the reports.
F. To forward to the Executive Safety Committee
recommendations for programs or projects initiated by the
Employee Safety Committee.
G. To coordinate compliance with federal, state and local safety
regulations.
H. To coordinate all materials necessary for and assist IRMA
with the LEAP evaluation.
IV. DEPARTMENT HEADS AND SUPERVISORS
Department Heads and Supervisors have full authority and
responsibility for creating and maintaining a safe and healthful work
environment within their departments. To achieve such a work
environment it is necessary to put into place working procedures
that will promote, to the highest degree possible, the safety of
municipal employees and that of the general public.
Department Heads and Supervisors may delegate authority and
assign responsibility to designees for many of the duties assigned
to them. They may not, however, delegate to another their
responsibility for accident prevention. Other specific responsibilities
include:

A. To develop and actively support a Departmental Safety
Program that will effectively control the frequency and
severity of accidents. This includes the scheduling of
regularly held safety training and awareness sessions at
which attendance by employees is mandatory.
B. To develop practical safety rules and regulations compatible
with the standard operating procedures of the department.
C. To ensure thorough and consistent job and safety training for
all employees assigned to or working for the department.
D. To monitor and enforce compliance with established safety
rules and procedures and discipline violators in accordance
with the provisions of the Member's Personnel Manual.
E. To establish, maintain and use to train employees a system
of job safety analyses.
F. To demonstrate, by example, good safety practices and a
positive attitude toward safety.
G. To conduct "tailgate sessions" for the purpose of planning
and laying out daily work assignments and to make frequent,
individual contacts with employees emphasizing potential
hazards and pointing out proper procedures for avoiding
them.
H. To inspect the design of new equipment and vehicles and to
ensure that operators have been properly trained before they
operate them.
I. To ensure that safety equipment, protective devices and
proper clothing are provided and used by employees in
accordance with Member policy.
J. To investigate thoroughly the causes of all accidents and to
take whatever action is necessary to prevent their
occurrence, even if there was no personal injury. All accident
and on-the-job injury reports and accompanying
documentation must be forwarded promptly to the Safety
Coordinator. The accurate, timely and complete preparation
and submission of the accident reports is measured along
with other components in evaluating a Supervisor's
performance.
K. To inform all employees, whether on permanent or
temporary assignment to the department, to report
immediately all injuries or accidents.
L. To provide first aid as necessary in case of a personal injury
and to arrange promptly for whatever medical attention is
necessary to treat the injury.

V. EMPLOYEES
As a condition of employment, each employee is responsible for
securing his or her own safety, the safety of fellow workers and that
of the general public to the extent to which the general public is
affected by an act carried out by a Member employee. Specific
duties include:
A. To accept willingly and support actively all approved safety
rules and/or procedures.
B. To anticipate safety hazards which can arise out of a
particular situation not contemplated by the written rules or
procedures.
C. To consult with a Supervisor before proceeding with a
particular job, if the appropriate procedure for handing the job
is questionable or unknown.
D. To concentrate on the job at hand, work on it at a reasonable
pace and use the safety precautions necessary to avoid
exposure to injury.
E. To notify a Supervisor promptly of an unsafe condition,
activity or procedure the employee has observed.
F. To participate actively in the Member's safety effort by
making safety suggestions either to the Departmental Safety
Committee Representative or to the Supervisor.
G. To keep work areas clean and orderly.
H. To use the proper tool(s) or equipment to do a job.
I. To operate no equipment without having obtained prior
authorization.
J. To refrain from engaging in horseplay which can lead to
serious injury and disciplinary action.
K. To avoid distracting others while they are at work.
L. To wear protective equipment as required either by rule (i.e.
wearing a hardhat when working in a designated hazardous
operations area), practice or common sense.
M. To arrive at work suitably attired for the job(s) to be
performed.
N. To cooperate with and assist in accident investigations by
identifying correctable causes and preventing their
recurrence.
To report promptly to a Supervisor all accidents and/or
injuries that have occurred within the scope of employment.

COMPONENTS OF RISK MANAGEMENT
I. SAFETY/ACCIDENT PREVENTION
The safety of Village employees and the public is of paramount
importance. Safety takes precedence over expedience or shortcuts.
Village employees are expected to be familiar and comply with all
safety procedures and policies established by the Village.
Emphasizing and promoting safety in the workplace, including safe
driving and the proper operation of equipment, is the first step in
managing risk. Safety procedures and policies are located in the
following documents:
A. The General Village Safety Policy is contained in the
Employee Handbook.
B. Safety policies specific to the nature of the job are also
detailed in Departmental SOP's (Standard Operating
Procedures).
C. Job Safety Analyses (JSA's). JSA's detail the proper
operational procedures for specific pieces of equipment.
D. Personal protective equipment is issued to all personnel for
their use.
Safety tips and reminders are periodically posted on each
department's bulletin board to underscore the importance of
performing one's job in a safe manner and maintaining safe policies
at home and away from work.
II. ACCIDENT REPORTING
All accidents that occur at work, including personal injuries that may
seem minor, are to be reported immediately to a Department Head
as soon as possible and before the end of the workday or shift. It is
the policy of the Village to report all damages to Village property.
Accident reports are submitted as follows:
A. Report forms are available from your Department Head.
There are two types of reports -- Personal Injury and Property
Damage.
For property damage claims, the IRMA Non-Workers
Compensation Accident Report Form must be completed.
For personal injury claims, employees should complete the
Employee's Statement of Injury Form. The Supervisor must
complete the Supervisor's Investigation Report.

For Workers Compensation claims, a "Form 45," Employer's
First Report of Injury or Illness, must also be submitted
before IRMA will establish a claim. For accidents that result in
time lost from work, a Workers Compensation Wage
Statement is also required and will be prepared by the Safety
Coordinator.
In some instances an employee may incur a strain or
exposure that does not require immediate medical attention,
but could require treatment. Such cases should be reported
to their Supervisor, the proper forms completed and filed with
the Safety Coordinator as "Information Only." Should
treatment be required and the cause linked to the work
incident, a Workers Comp claim could be filed.
(Note: The Village follows the IRMA Reporting Guidelines
and Claim Handling Protocol for Bloodborne Pathogen
Exposure in order to maintain the confidentiality of the
claimant.)
B. Fully completed forms must be submitted to the Safety
Coordinator.
C. Upon review and the addition of supplemental information as
needed, claim forms are faxed to IRMA. Claims Coordinator,
coordinates all workers comp claims as well as all other
accident and liability claims. IRMA requires that claims be
submitted within five (5) workdays of the incident. It is
imperative to report and process claims immediately.
D. Medical Management Network. The proper care and
treatment of work-related injuries is a primary concern for
the Village. Therefore, Stickney participates in the IRMA
Medical Management Network (MMN). The MMN is
designed to provide quality care and reduce the Workers
Comp loss costs to the Village. The Medical Management
facility for the Village of Stickney is MacNeal Clearing Clinic
from Monday, 5 a.m. to Saturday, 12 noon and MacNeal
Hospital Emergency from Saturday, 12 noon to Monday, 5
a.m.
E. If damage is done to Village property, Safety coordinator will
coordinate IRMA inspections and notify the department when
IRMA has approved repairs.
(Note: In vehicle accident cases a visual inspection of the
damaged vehicle must be made by IRMA if the damage to
the Village vehicle is over $2,500.00 and of a private vehicle
if the damage is over $2,500.00.

III. CLAIMS ANALYSIS
Each quarter IRMA provides the Village with a report of losses. The
report breaks down all claims by frequency and dollar amount. The
Quarterly Loss Report is reviewed by the Risk Manager and
summarized for the Village Board and Claims and Safety Coordinator.
The Safety Coordinator reviews the Quarterly Loss Report with the
Executive Safety Committee. Claim history is reviewed at the Executive
Safety Meeting for the purpose of analyzing trends and identifying
solutions.
IV. UNSAFE CONDITIONS
In order to meet the Village's risk management objectives, each
employee is reminded to be on the lookout for potential unsafe
conditions in the workplace, with equipment, on public property or in
public rights-of-way. Unsafe conditions can be reported by completing
the Unsafe Conditions Report Form or by advising your Supervisor.
V. GENERAL LIABILITY
General Liability covers private parties who wish to make a claim for
damages against the Village. Typical cases include slips and falls on
public property, sewer backups, damage to property by Village
employees and lawsuits against the Village. The Claims Coordinator
coordinates general liability claims. Anyone seeking to file a claim
should see the safety coordinator. .
VI. CONTRACTUAL RISK MANAGEMENT AND TRANSFER OF RISK
Contractual risk management involves the transfer of risk through a
contract from the Village to the contracting party. In general, anyone
contracting with the Village should provide the Village with a certificate
of insurance at an acceptable amount naming the Village of Stickney,
its officials, agents, employees and volunteers as an additional insured.
In addition, an indemnification may be required and the contract will
include language limiting or transferring the Village's level of risk.
Anyone preparing or managing contracts should be familiar with risk
avoidance provisions.
VII. HEALTH/DISEASE PREVENTION
An often overlooked component of managing risk is the practice of
making healthy lifestyle choices. It is in the best interest of the Village
to promote healthy lifestyles. The Village does this by making several
optional programs available to employees at no cost.
May 2005
