title: Property-Valuables
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish a process by which all valuables found at emergency incidents
are inventoried and held securely by the Department until the items can be returned to the owner or
otherwise legally released for disposition.
POLICY:
The Stickney Fire Department will take reasonable measures to safeguard valuables found at incident
scenes. The Department does not have appropriate facilities for storing valuables for safekeeping.
Therefore, alternatives to removing valuables from the scene of emergencies will be taken whenever
practicable.
I. PROCEDURE
A. Unsecured valuables refers to the those items such as cash, jewelry, or other property
that are found on a scene that is a locale other than the patient's residence or place of
domicile.
B. Any member encountering unsecured valuables, such as cash or jewelry, should
immediately report it to the officer or acting officer on duty.
C. When local law enforcement is available, valuable property should be transferred to legal
custody with law enforcement on the scene. The member transferring the property shall
obtain a receipt/documentation of custody from the law enforcement official.
D. If the valuables cannot be secured and they belong to a medical patient who is
transported to a hospital, the member may deliver the valuables to the hospital. The
member shall document the items delivered to the hospital and the name of the
individual that the items were delivered to.
E. If the property or valuables cannot be secured at the location or with a responsible person
at the scene, the member should request a law enforcement officer to the scene to take
the valuables for safekeeping. The member shall document the disposition of such
valuables, including the identity of any receiving individual and include it in the report of
the incident.
F. A member should take valuables into custody only in unusual cases and with the approval
of the of officer or acting officer on duty.

G. Any valuable taken into custody by the fire department shall be documented for
identification, existing damage, and the names of those members involved in securing the
items.
H. Property shall be securely stored.
I. The stored property may be released to the property’s owner upon presentation of
appropriate identification. The property release shall be documented in a report.
II. PROPERTY AUDITS/INSPECTIONS
A. Annually, the Fire Chief shall designate an officer to conduct a complete audit of any
property in the Department’s custody.
B. Twice a year, the Fire Chief shall order an inspection of any secured property areas for
cleanliness and proper compliance with these procedures.
C. A report of the audit or inspection shall be submitted to the Fire Chief.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Funerals
body:
PURPOSE:
It is the intent of this policy to ensure that every member of the Department, both active and retired, who
passes away may be offered the option of a funeral or assistance from the Department. These guidelines
will ensure proper support and care of the family and the posthumous honoring of a member of the
Department.
POLICY:
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department for the Fire Chief or the authorized designee to make the
necessary assignments and coordinate actions with other department representatives any time the
Department learns that an active or retired employee has passed away. Activities should be in accordance
with the Line-of-Duty Death, Line-of-Duty Death and Injury Notification and Family Support Liaison
policies.
If a responsible family member requests department assistance, the Fire Chief or authorized designee
should appoint, with the approval of the family member, an employee to act as a funeral detail officer
and oversee all of the arrangements. The Fire Chief may deny the option of department participation if
the circumstances of the member’s death may reasonably bring discredit to the Department.
The Fire Chief or the authorized designee should determine the highest level of participation the
Department can provide, based on the cause of death.
I. DEFINITIONS
Definitions developed by the Illinois Fire Chiefs Association (IFCA) and related to this policy
include:
A. Active member – A full-time member or volunteer member of fire or EMS services in an
active capacity.
B. Inactive member – A retired, former or pensioned member of a fire or EMS service.
C. Affiliate member – An individual who has served in some capacity with the department,
such as commissioner, trustee, dispatcher, etc.
II. LEVEL OF PARTICIPATION
A. The desires of the family are paramount and shall be given fullest consideration.
B. The IFCA offers guidance and planning assistance with funerals and has available Fire
Service Funeral Guidelines for consideration. The IFCA recommends that departments
adopt their own funeral protocol, prior to needing it, in order to create consistency.

III. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The Fire Chief or the authorized designee may appoint one or more of the following
positions to provide assistance with the funeral arrangements:
1. Family Support Liaison - Any department member who is a close friend of the
family and will make reasonable efforts to address the needs and desires of the
family, communicate between the Department and the family and coordinate
details with the Officer in Charge (OIC).
2. Funeral detail officer - An employee who is appointed by the Fire Chief to oversee
all arrangements for a funeral.
3. Head usher - The head usher is responsible for seating and parking arrangements
at the funeral services, both at the church and at the grave site.
4. Honor Guard Commander/Officer in Charge of the Honor Guard and pipe and
drum band - This position will be filled by a member of the Honor Guard and will
be responsible for the coordination of the Honor Guard, Color Guard and the pipe
and drum band.
5. Honorary pallbearers - Honorary pallbearers are those selected by the family.
They will follow the casket from the location of the services to the grave site.
6. Logistics officer - The logistics officer is charged with preparing the apparatus,
vehicles, equipment and facilities for the funeral services.
7. Officer in Charge (OIC)/detail officer - Selected by the Fire Chief or the authorized
designee, the detail officer is the person in charge of the overall department
participation and is responsible for the coordination between the funeral
director, the chaplain and the family support liaison.
8. Public agency liaison (as needed) - The public agency liaison will coordinate any
interaction with other public agencies that wish to participate in the services.
9. Public Information Officer (as needed) - The Public Information Officer will
coordinate all media and public relations issues.
10. Pallbearers - The pallbearers will be members of the Honor Guard, unless
otherwise requested by the family.
11. Protocol liaison - Appointed by the Fire Chief or the authorized designee, the
protocol liaison will provide direction, advice and clarification to the family
regarding proper funeral procedures.
12. Transportation officer - The transportation officer is responsible for all
transportation of family members, pallbearers and escort detail from a predetermined location to the location of the services, from the service to the grave
site and back to a pre-determined location (e.g., the family home, place of
worship).
IV. FUNERAL PROCEDURES
A. Members who attend the funeral services will report to a pre-designated assembly point
near the place of services for inspection and briefing.

B. From the assembly point, members will proceed to the place of service, timing their
arrival to permit immediate entry upon the arrival of the deceased officer.
C. Upon entering the church or synagogue, members will remove their uniform hats and
place them under their left arm, hat brim forward and will move in an orderly manner to
the place that is reserved for them.
D. Members will remain standing until all members are in their places, at which time the
command “BE SEATED” is given.
E. Members will sit with their hats upright in their laps and will maintain a military bearing
throughout the service.
F. At the end of the service, upon receiving the command of “ALL RISE”, members will rise
in unison and place their hats under their left arm and prepare to file past the casket.
Members will hold their hats in this position until they pass the casket and walk outside.
G. Upon leaving the building, members will replace their hats and assemble in formation at
right angles to the hearse.
1. Two ranks will be formed facing each other, leaving an aisle through which the
pallbearers and the casket will pass.
2. Members will be formed according to height in two separate groups; those
wearing a dress coat and those not wearing a dress coat. They will be normally
dressed at extended intervals but may be dressed at close intervals if space is
limited.
3. While waiting in formation, members will stand at parade rest.
H. When the casket comes into view, the formation will be called to attention. The next
command will be “PRESENT ARMS”. All members will salute and will hold the salute until
the casket is placed into the hearse. At this time, commands of “READY, FRONT” will be
given and members will return to attention.
I. After the doors of the hearse are closed, the command of “FIRST RANK (Passenger side of
hearse) RIGHT FACE” and “SECOND RANK (Driver’s side of hearse) LEFT FACE,” will be
given so the two columns are facing the hearse.
J. The Honor Guard Coordinator will then dismiss the formation with the command of
“DISMISSED”. The members will then break ranks in an orderly manner and proceed to
their vehicles.
K. Members will then proceed in the motorcade to the cemetery.
V. GRAVESITE SERVICES
A. Members will report to the places that have been reserved for them immediately upon
arrival at the gravesite. If indoors, members will remove their hats and hold them under
their left arm. If seated, members will sit with their hats in their laps. If services are
outside, members will wear hats. At all times, members will maintain a military bearing.
B. Prior to the playing of “TAPS” and the three-round rifle volley, members will be given the
command of “ALL RISE” (if seated) at which time members will rise. The next command
given will be the command of “PRESENT ARMS”, at which time a hand salute will be
rendered.

C. At this time the Honor Guard Coordinator will instruct the members of the Honor Guard
to fold the flag. Once folded, the Honor Guard Coordinator will turn the flag over to a
Chief Officer and will salute the flag. The Chief Officer will then repeat this process and
turn the flag over to the Fire Chief. At this time, the Chief will present the flag to the
surviving family members.
D. At this time the three-round rifle volley will be rendered. Once this is concluded, “TAPS”
will be played. Upon the conclusion of “TAPS”, the command of “READY FRONT” will be
given at which time members will return to the position of attention. The Honor Guard
Coordinator will then give the command of “DISMISSED”. At this time, members will break
ranks and return to their assigned vehicles.
VI. PROCEDURAL VARIATION
A. The procedures that have been outlined in this Order will be followed in most cases.
B. Any changes that are made necessary by shortage of manpower, the unusual size of the
funeral, the type of service, the physical arrangement of the place of the service or for
any other reasons, shall be made by the Department Liaison Officer in conjunction with
the Fire Chief.
C. At the discretion of the Fire Chief, Department Honors may be accorded to
deceased/retired members of the Department and employees.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Fire Inspections Program
body:
PURPOSE:
This policy provides guidance for the enforcement of fire codes through periodic inspection within
Stickney Fire Department’s jurisdiction. Additionally, this policy establishes the minimum standards for
inspection frequencies of all buildings in the department’s jurisdiction.
POLICY:
The Stickney Fire Department is committed to improving public safety through the enforcement of
building standards relating to fire and public safety as adopted by the Illinois Office of the State Fire
Marshal (OSFM) and published in the Illinois Fire Code, and any other regulations or ordinances that have
been formally adopted by the OSFM or the Village for the prevention of fire or the protection of life and
property against fire (425 ILCS 25/9; 41 Ill. Adm. Code 100.7).
I. RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The Fire Chief or the authorized designee shall develop a periodic inspection program
based on the risks to life and property for occupancies within the Stickney Fire
Department’s jurisdictional boundaries.
B. The inspection program will comply with the Illinois Fire Code and any local amendments
or ordinances specific to the Village.
C. The Department fire inspection program will be administered by the Fire Investigation
Team Division under the responsibility of the Fire Chief.
D. All fire department personnel will be responsible to notify the appropriate supervisor
and/or the Inspectional Services Division when any of the following conditions are found
involving any building (commercial, industrial or residential) within the Village while in
the course of their duties and responsibilities:
1. Fire protection systems that have a trouble indication or have been taken out of
service due to mechanical or electrical failure (Commercial/Industrial only).
Physical damage to fire department connections (FDC), standpipes or blocked
access to FDCs and fire protections systems.
2. Building and Life Safety Code violations which if uncorrected pose an immediate
threat to life safety and property – Health code violations, obstructed egress,
exposed, damaged or unprotected utilities (gas, water, electric), etc.

3. Building structural integrity issues due to weather, impact, water leak, fire or
natural deterioration, which may result in structural failure endangering life
safety and property.
4. Building fires resulting in substantial damage to structural members or utility
components (gas, electric, water).
5. Any construction or service work being completed without proper building
permits.
6. Any conditions not covered by this policy in which at the discretion of the
employee may pose a reasonable threat to life safety and property.
II. INSPECTION PROGRAM GUIDELINES
A. The Fire Chief or his/her designee shall develop an inspection program based on
community risk reduction through education and enforcement. Inspections should be
identified by risk, hazard, occupancy, frequency, and required state law and local code or
ordinance.
B. JAILS AND DETENTION FACILITIES
1. Jail or detention facility inspections shall be made at least once every two years
for compliance with the regulations adopted by the Illinois Fire Code and the
minimum standards pertaining to fire and life-safety as adopted by the Illinois
Department of Corrections.
2. Reports of all jail or detention facility inspections shall be submitted to the facility
manager of the jail or detention facility, the local governing body and the
Department of Corrections within 30 days of the inspection.
C. APARTMENTS, HOTELS AND MOTELS
1. All structures subject to state and local fire codes, except dwellings, shall be
inspected annually for compliance with building standards and other state and
local regulations.
D. SCHOOLS
1. The Stickney Fire Department shall inspect every building used as a public or
private school in the department’s jurisdiction not less than once each year as
delegated by the State Fire Marshal (41 Ill. Adm. Code 111.40), and as required
by the Illinois State Board of Education.
a) The Prevention Services Division shall be responsible for scheduling all
school safety inspections through the Regional Office of Education.
b) The Prevention Services Division shall assign a qualified inspector to
conduct the annual school safety inspection. This inspector may be
released from regular duty for the duration of the inspection.
c) Inspectors assigned to perform annual school safety inspections are
responsible for completing all documentation and filing it with the
Prevention Services Division.
d) The inspector shall enter a record of the completed inspection into the
department’s internal records.

2. The results of any inspection shall be sent to the regional school superintendent
or authorized designee. The OSFM shall be notified of any violations that present
imminent harm to occupants of the school and of any violations that are not
corrected by the next annual fire inspection (41 Ill. Adm. Code 111.90).
E. HIGH-RISE BUILDINGS
1. The Stickney Fire Department shall annually inspect all high-rise structures in its
jurisdiction for compliance with building standards and other state and local
regulations.
2. The results of the inspection shall be submitted to the facility manager in an
appropriate form no later than 30 days after the date of the inspection.
3. The definition of a high-rise structure is any building more than 75 feet tall
measured from the lowest point accessible by department vehicles to the floor
of the highest story that is designed for occupancy. This shall be the threshold for
the activation of the high-rise incident command structure. (See Policy 309 - High-
Rise Incident Management).
F. HAZARDOUS OCCUPANCIES
1. Facilities that handle, store or use hazardous materials shall be inspected for
compliance with applicable provisions of the state and local codes and ordinances
as well as the accuracy of any required hazardous materials business plan.
2. Facilities that are required to submit a hazardous materials business plan shall be
inspected no less frequently than once every three years.
G. RIGHT OF ENTRY
1. If a building or premise to be inspected is occupied, the inspector shall present
credentials to the occupant and request entry. If the building or premise is
unoccupied, the inspector shall first make a reasonable effort to locate the owner
or other person having charge or control of the building or premise and request
entry (425 ILCS 25/9).
2. If no permission to enter is granted, the inspector should work with legal counsel
to secure entry in a manner provided by law, such as obtaining an administrative
search warrant.
III. INSPECTION FEES
A. The Department may charge any fire inspection fees adopted by the Village. The fee
assessed shall not exceed the estimated reasonable cost of providing the service for which
the fee is charged.
B. If a violation is discovered during an inspection, the follow-up inspection to ensure the
corrections have been made should be conducted at no cost to the owner or occupant.
Should the owner or occupant fail to comply with inspection requirements on the followup visit and an additional visit is required, a fee as adopted by the Village may be assessed.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Permits
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide guidance for issuing permits that are required by the Illinois Fire
Code (41 Ill. Adm. Code 100.7) and local ordinances.
POLICY:
In order to provide for the safety of the community, it is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department that
permit requirements are appropriately observed and enforced.
I. PERMIT PROCESS
A. A list of permits requiring approval should be available to the public and upon request.
The Department shall provide adequate guidance to assist the public in obtaining
approval for a particular permit.
B. An inspection shall be conducted prior to permit issuance.
C. A permit does not constitute authority to violate, cancel or set aside any of the provisions
of the Illinois Fire Code or other applicable regulations or local ordinance.
D. Permits are generally required for all items, locations and activities as described in the
Illinois Fire Code and applicable local ordinances.
II. PERMIT APPLICATIONS
A. Applications for permits should be submitted to the Fire Marshal or the authorized
designee and should include adequate documentation of the intent to comply, including,
but not limited to:
1. A site plan showing the location of storage, use, handling or processes associated
with the permit.
2. The floor plan approved by the Stickney Fire Department depicting the storage of
hazardous materials and the use of equipment or processes, including proof of
compliance with all applicable codes and standards.
3. A current hazardous materials emergency plan, if applicable.
4. A chemical classification inventory, if applicable.
B. PERMIT FEES - Permit fees should be collected at the time of application. The fees are
established by the Village governing body and are applicable to each permit application.

III. PERMIT ISSUANCE
A. A permit may be issued for a specific or an indefinite period of time, depending on the
circumstances. A permit may be extended upon showing good cause if the permittee
applies for an extension in writing before the expiration of the permit. A permit is not
transferable. Any change in ownership, operation, occupancy or use shall require a new
permit.
B. Construction permits shall automatically become invalid unless the work authorized by
such permit is commenced within 180 days after its issuance or if the work is suspended
or abandoned for a period of 180 days after the time the work is commenced.
C. All permits shall bear the signature of the Fire Chief or the authorized designee and
contain a general description of the operation or occupancy and its location.
IV. SITE REQUIREMENTS
A. Permits should be posted in a visible location at the permitted premises or in a location
approved by the Fire Chief or the authorized designee.
B. Permits are subject to inspection at any time by any firefighter acting in an official
capacity.
V. SUSPENDED OR REVOKED PERMITS
A. Permits may be suspended or revoked any time it is determined that:
1. The permit is being used by someone other than the person who was issued the
permit.
2. The permit is being used at a location other than the permitted location.
3. Any condition of the permit has been violated.
4. The work being performed is out of compliance with applicable code
requirements.
5. The permit was obtained by the use of false statements on the application.
6. The issuance of the permit was an error or in violation of a regulation, code or
law.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Code Enforcement
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish the process by which the Stickney Fire Department will enforce
Village fire and life-safety codes during inspections.
POLICY:
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to use inspections to help reduce the risk of injury or death
due to fire and life-safety code-related violations, and increase the safety of building occupants, the
community and emergency responders.
I. PROCEDURE
A. The Stickney Fire Department may issue correction notices when violations of the fire
code and local ordinances are found during fire and life-safety inspections.
B. Any violation determined by an inspector to pose an immediate fire danger or threat to
life-safety should be referred to the Fire Marshal as soon as practicable.
C. Correction notices shall be issued to the owner, occupant or other interested person
either in person or via certified mail (425 ILCS 25/9).
II. INSPECTIONS
A. INITIAL INSPECTIONS
1. An initial inspection should be made to determine if any violations exist and to
identify the code sections violated. A notice of correction shall be issued for
violations. The written correction notice shall describe the conditions deemed to
be unsafe, identify the code section violated and, when compliance is not
immediate, specify a time for re-inspection, typically to occur within two weeks.
This time frame may be adjusted at the inspector’s discretion and based on the
type of violation.
2. All inspections, meetings and telephone conversations should be documented
and an inspection report completed including names, telephone numbers, dates,
violations and any other pertinent information related to the inspection. All
documentation should be maintained in an inspection file.
3. A copy of the inspection report will be left with the responsible party.

B. RE-INSPECTIONS
1. Violations that pose an immediate hazard to life or property should be corrected
before the inspector leaves the premises (e.g., a required exit being chained or
locked).
2. All other violations should be corrected by the date identified in the correction
notice for re- inspection.
3. Generally, no more than two re-inspections should be conducted before
escalating the process as provided in this policy.
C. TIME EXTENSIONS FOR COMPLIANCE
1. An inspector may extend the compliance period if reasonable progress is being
made toward correcting the violation, or if a plan is established for completion
and life and property are not being compromised.
2. Extensions should only be granted when the inspector believes there is a high
probability of obtaining complete compliance.
3. The inspector may request the responsible person submit a statement in writing
detailing the reason for the extension and the new compliance date.
D. FINAL NOTICES
1. A final notice may be used as the last warning notice issued prior to civil or
criminal action.
2. A final notice is not required prior to initiating legal action.
3. A final notice of violation should be provided to the violator by service of the
order upon the owner, occupant, or other person interested in the premises shall
be in person, by electronic transmission, or by registered or certified mail and
should:
a) Set a date by which the violator must correct the violation.
b) Notify the violator of the date of the final re-inspection to verify code
compliance prior to initiating legal action.
III. ADMINISTRATIVE CITATION
A. If compliance is not achieved by the time of the final re-inspection, an administrative
citation may be issued. An administrative citation informs a business that repeated
attempts to gain compliance for outstanding violations were unsuccessful. The
administrative citation may be delivered to the business owner in person, by electronic
transmission, or mailed via certified mail return receipt requested.
B. Administrative citations may continue to be issued until compliance is achieved or the
matter is referred to legal counsel for legal action. Copies of all administrative citations
should be sent to the department's legal counsel as soon as practicable.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Community Fire Station Visitation Program
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish the methods the Department uses to interact with the
community, share information about the workings of a fire station and demonstrate the capabilities of
various apparatus and equipment through educational activities conducted by the Operations Division.
POLICY:
The Stickney Fire Department will aggressively promote fire safety and public awareness through a variety
of public information and education activities, including a fire station visit program operated by the
Operations Division.
http://www.stickneyfire.com/index.php/public-education
I. PROCEDURE
A. The fire station visit program is an educational activity intended to allow school groups,
service clubs, youth organizations, church groups and other civic-minded organizations to
schedule and participate in a tour of a working fire station. The types of groups and
organizations appropriate for inclusion in the fire station visit program include, but are
not limited to:
1. Pre-school classes or groups (public or private).
2. Kindergarten classes or groups (public or private).
3. Primary and secondary school groups (public, church-based or private).
4. Chaperoned, organized youth groups that generally include persons 17 years of
age and under and are sponsored and accompanied by adult representatives of a
formal organization (e.g., Girl Scouts, Boy Scouts, Cub Scouts, Indian Scouts,
Brownies).
5. Service clubs and organizations that are generally voluntary non-profit
organizations, where members meet regularly to perform charitable work either
by direct hands-on efforts or by raising money for other organizations (e.g.,
Kiwanis, Rotary, Masons).
B. The fire station visit program is not intended, nor should it be used, as an entertainment
opportunity or for a commercial or for-profit purpose. The following types of groups,
entities and activities are not appropriate for inclusion in the fire station visit program:

1. Birthday party groups
2. Social networking groups
3. Business networking groups
4. For-profit tour groups, including profit-based foreign student groups
5. Any group, entity or activity that is part of a for-profit enterprise
C. Neither of the lists above is intended to be all-inclusive, rather they are general
representations of the types of groups that are either appropriate or inappropriate for
inclusion in the fire station visit program.
D. Groups or organizations can request a fire station visit by completing and submitting an
application to the Fire Investigation Team Division. Applications must be submitted at
least 45 days prior to the date requested for the fire station visit. Fire Investigation Team
Division personnel will evaluate each application in accordance with this policy. Each
evaluation will be considered uniformly and without discrimination as part of the
application process. Approved applications will be forwarded to the appropriate
Operations Chief for station and crew assignment.
E. The fire station visit program will operate within the following parameters:
1. Participating group size will generally be limited to 30 persons, including
chaperones and drivers. Larger groups may apply but approval of the application
will depend on the availability of a Fire Investigation Team Division representative
to assist with managing the tour on the day of the visit.
2. Station visits should be scheduled for a maximum of two hours and generally
during regular business hours.
3. The crew assigned to manage a station visit should remain in-service and available
for emergency calls during the visit. Visiting groups should be notified in advance
that the crew may be called away from the station at any time and the visit may
then be canceled.
4. Station visit participants shall not be allowed to enter the private crew sleeping
or dressing areas of the station.
5. Participants shall not be allowed to climb on or into fire apparatus unless
chaperoned by a member of the Stickney Fire Department.
6. The fire crews managing each station visit shall ensure that no confidential
information or information protected by the Health Insurance Portability and
Accountability Act (HIPAA) is visible or accessible to the station visit participants.
Specific areas of the station may be closed to the visiting groups as needed to
protect confidential and/or protected materials.
7. If an unforeseen event occurs in which a visitor falls or injures him/herself during
a station visit, the on-duty crew will handle the incident as an Emergency Medical
Services (EMS) event.
II. 404.3.1 SCHEDULING FIRE STATION VISITS
A. To limit the impact of fire station visits on other essential activities, each Operations
Division crew should be limited to conducting one station visit per calendar month.

B. The Operations Chief may elect to further limit the number of station visits assigned to
individual crews based on the operational or training activities of that crew.
C. The Chief will notify the Fire Investigation Team Division personnel of the station and crew
assigned to conduct each scheduled visit.
D. The Fire Investigation Team Division personnel shall confirm the appointment for the
station visit with the applicant and act as the point of contact for the applicant regarding
any questions, issues or changes in the scheduled visit.
III. RECORD KEEPING
A. The Fire Investigation Team Division should maintain a record of all applications for the
station visit program. The records should include:
1. (a) The name of the group or organization applying for a fire station visit.
2. (b) The name of the group leader or person submitting the application.
3. (c) Information regarding the approval or denial of the application. For
denied applications, the reason for the denial should be listed (e.g., nonconforming group, scheduling conflict, no crew availability).
4. (d) The scheduled date and time of each approved visit.
5. (e) The Officer in Charge, station and crew assigned to manage the visit.
6. (f) Confirmation that the group or organization completed the station visit
or the reason it was not completed.
B. These records should be retained in accordance with the department’s established
records retention schedules.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Fireworks Displays
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish general guidelines for the use of pyrotechnic devices in public
fireworks displays to ensure that minimum life-safety procedures and practices are followed. The policy
also outlines the Stickney Fire Department standards for the storage and disposal of illegal fireworks (425
ILCS 35/0.01 et seq.).
POLICY
Fireworks are energetic materials that are inherently dangerous and should always be handled with
caution. Heat, shock and friction may ignite them, and in all cases, safety should be the primary concern.
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to observe the Illinois Pyrotechnic Use Act and follow the
regulations prepared by the local, state or regional authorities governing the use of fireworks in public
displays when enforcing permitting requirements, plan review and inspections (425 ILCS 35/2.1; 425 ILCS
35/2.2; 41 Ill. Adm. Code 235). The Department shall observe the federal regulations governing the
storage and disposal of explosives (27 CFR 555, Subpart K).
I. PERMITTING PROCESS
A. Applications for permits for public fireworks displays shall be made in writing at least 15
days prior to the proposed display. Applications shall be submitted to the Stickney Fire
Department in a timely manner in order to ensure the appropriate allocation of resources
and to allow adequate time to address any changes that may be required (425 ILCS 35/2.1;
425 ILCS 35/2.2; 41 Ill. Adm. Code 235.40; 41 Ill. Adm. Code 235.60).
B. When applying for public fireworks display permit, an applicant shall submit information
and evidence to the Stickney Fire Department that includes:
1. The name of the organization sponsoring the display, and the names and
pyrotechnic operator license numbers of persons actually in charge of the display.
2. The date and time the display is to be held.
3. The exact location planned for the display.
4. The size and number of all fireworks to be discharged including the number of set
pieces, shells and other items. Shells shall be designated by diameter specifying
single, multiple break or salute.
5. The manner and place of storage of all fireworks prior to, during and after the
display.

6. A diagram of the grounds on which the display is to be held showing:
a) The point at which the fireworks are to be discharged.
b) The location of all buildings, roads and other lines of communication.
c) The lines behind which the audience will be restrained.
7. The location of all nearby trees, telegraph or telephone lines, or any other
overhead obstruction.
8. Proof that satisfactory workers’ compensation insurance is carried for all
employees.
9. Documentary proof of liability insurance in a sum not less than $1,000,000 (425
ILCS 35/2.1).
10. Identification of a licensed lead pyrotechnic operator employed by a licensed
pyrotechnic distributor or a licensed production company that will be conducting
the display (425 ILCS 35/2.1) and who has received training approved by the
Office of the State Fire Marshal (425 ILCS 35/2.2).
11. The name and resale license number of the wholesaler who supplied all of the
items used in the display.
C. The permittee shall be responsible for compliance with the provisions under which a
public fireworks display permit has been granted. A letter is required from the sponsor or
pyrotechnic company acknowledging that any additional fees will be billed directly to the
sponsor or company. Public displays fired on private property must also include a letter
from the current property owner approving the event and holding the Stickney Fire
Department, its officers and the Village harmless for any damages or liability.
II. PLANS
A. A fully dimensioned plot plan shall be included with the application that shows:
1. The location of the display set-up and the location, including the distance of the
firing box from the display.
2. All access roads, including road width, hydrant locations and ingress and egress
points.
3. All structures located in or near the firing area and a fallout area based upon 100
feet per inch of shell size.
III. INSPECTIONS
A. All department personnel involved in the inspection of any public fireworks display setup and firing shall inspect for compliance with 41 Ill. Adm. Code 235.100 and 41 Ill. Adm.
Code 235.25.
B. All inspections will be documented and filed in the administrative records. Violations shall
be reported to the Fire Chief.
IV. STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF ILLEGAL FIREWORKS
A. Any fireworks collected pursuant to state law shall be stored in a manner approved by
the Stickney Fire Department Fire Prevention Bureau until relinquished to the local state
or regional authorities for destruction.

B. The Stickney Fire Department Fire Prevention Chief or the authorized designee shall notify
the local, state or regional authorities as soon as practicable and include the quantity,
type and location of the fireworks. Collected fireworks shall be disposed of as directed by
the by the Fire Prevention Bureau.
1. Small amounts (quantities that are temporarily manageable):
a) Inventory, randomly sample and photograph the collected fireworks.
b) Complete any forms required by the appropriate authority and forward
as the form instructs.
c) If the fireworks are in the original U.S. Department of Transportation
(DOT) shipping cartons, do not remove.
d) Loose fireworks must be placed in good quality cardboard boxes, such as
banker boxes, the boxes that photocopy paper comes in or similarly sized
moving boxes. The boxes must have functional lids.
e) The boxes must be labeled with the following information: type of
fireworks, agency’s name, person responsible for the sorting and the
date.
f) The following items should not be included:
(1) Improvised Explosive Devices (IED) and explosives (a bomb squad
should handle these)
(2) Trash (including expended fireworks, lighters and matches)
(3) Any evidence or contraband that is not related to fireworks (e.g.,
weapons, drugs, paraphernalia)
(4) Friction-initiated fireworks (e.g., Snap Caps) should be packaged
separately from any other items
2. Large amounts that require immediate assistance (quantities that exceed the
capability of the Stickney Fire Department to manage):
a) Contact the State Fire Marshal investigator, who will assist with arranging
for temporary storage.
b) Inventory, randomly sample and photograph the collected fireworks.
c) Complete the necessary report and forward it to the appropriate
authority.
d) If the fireworks are in the original U.S. DOT shipping cartons, do not
remove them.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Maximum Occupancy - Overcrowding
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish standards for abating overcrowded conditions in places of
assembly. This policy shall apply to all assembly occupancies and other occupancies which may be subject
to overcrowding pursuant to the Illinois Fire Code (41 Ill. Adm. Code 100.7).
POLICY
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to protect the safety of the public through enforcement of
the Illinois Fire Code regarding occupancy overcrowding.
I. 407.3 ENFORCEMENT
A. Any member of the Department, upon finding overcrowded conditions beyond the
approved capacity of a building or portion thereof, or obstructions in aisles, passageways
or other means of egress, or upon finding any condition which constitutes a life-safety
hazard, is authorized to order the dangerous condition removed or remedied (425 ILCS
25/9).
B. The investigating officer shall immediately notify the Fire Marshal any time the decision
is made to vacate an occupancy.
C. Whenever practicable, the investigating officer should consult the Fire Marshal prior to
requiring that an occupancy be vacated.
II. COMPLAINTS
A. COMPLAINTS RECEIVED DURING NORMAL BUSINESS HOURS
1. All routine complaints of overcrowded conditions shall be forwarded to the Fire
Investigation Team Division for investigation and follow-up.
2. The complaint shall be entered into the complaint management system as soon
as practicable and shall be assigned to an available inspector.
3. The inspector should promptly investigate the complaint and notify the
appropriate supervisor of the findings.
4. All findings shall be documented in the complaint management system.
5. All overcrowding hazards should be mitigated as necessary, in accordance with
this policy.

B. COMPLAINTS RECEIVED AFTER HOURS
1. All complaints of overcrowding received by Dispatch after hours shall be routed
to the appropriate on-duty Officer in Charge.
2. Depending upon the urgency of the complaint, the Officer in Charge may choose
to take any of the following actions, as deemed necessary to investigate the
complaint:
a) Investigate the complaint and abate the hazard as necessary, in
accordance with this policy.
b) Dispatch an engine company to investigate the complaint and abate the
hazard as necessary, in accordance with this policy.
c) Call for assistance from the Fire Marshal, who should investigate the
complaint and abate the hazard as necessary, in accordance with this
policy.
d) Call for local law enforcement support.
III. OFFENSES
A. FIRST DOCUMENTED OVERCROWDING OFFENSE
1. Routine overcrowding complaints that do not pose an immediate life-safety
hazard should be investigated and abated as necessary, in accordance with
established procedures.
2. A warning letter should be issued to the business owner advising that any future
overcrowding cases may result in a criminal citation being issued.
B. SECOND DOCUMENTED OVERCROWDING OFFENSE
1. The second and all subsequent documented cases of overcrowding should result
in a criminal citation being issued, in accordance with Stickney Fire Department
procedures.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Juvenile Fire Setter Referrals
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide department personnel with resources for helping juvenile fire
setters and their families receive the help they need through education, diversion, assessment and
psychological services, in cooperation with local nonprofit organizations.
POLICY:
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to participate in a coordinated effort with local nonprofit
organizations and the Illinois Fire Safety Alliance’s (IFSA) Juvenile Fire Setter Intervention Program (JFSIP)
to provide appropriate referral or treatment services to juveniles from this jurisdiction.
In qualifying members to act as interventionists, the Stickney Fire Department recognizes training
provided by IFSA and its JFSIP certification courses as the only training recognized by the Illinois Office of
the State Fire Marshal (OSFM), and as a credible means of preparing interventionists for their interactions
with juvenile fire setters.
I. REFERRALS
A. Entry into a juvenile fire setter program may be recommended by department personnel
following a request from parents, guardians or caregivers, or as a result of a fire incident.
Upon referral of a juvenile fire setter, the IFSA office or the JFSIP help line should be
contacted to obtain a case number.
B. There are multiple types of referrals:
1. CAREGIVER REFERRALS - Parents or guardians who call the Stickney Fire
Department for assistance will be directed to a member trained in juvenile fire
setter intervention. When possible, telephone contact should be made with the
parents within 48 hours of the Department being contacted. Parents should be
provided with information about the program options and should be encouraged
to make an appointment with the department’s Fire Investigation Team
personnel. A pre-interview form should be completed during the telephone
contact.
2. WALK-IN REFERRALS - If someone comes to a fire station with a child who may be
involved with fire setting, that person should be referred to Fire Investigation
Team. If no Fire Investigation Team personnel are available, a pre-interview
referral form should be completed during the walk-in contact and forwarded to
the Fire Investigation Team Division. When appropriate, a Fire Investigation Team

member should be contacted to advise of the walk-in contact and asked to return
to the station, if possible.
3. FIRE DEPARTMENT REFERRALS - If a juvenile fire setter is identified at a fire scene,
the Incident Commander (IC) should complete a juvenile fire setter referral form.
The form should be forwarded to the Fire Investigation Team Division. The IC
should be contacted by the Fire Investigation Team Division confirming the
receipt of the referral form and advising what action is being taken with the
juvenile and his/her family.
a) If evidence at a fire scene indicates a juvenile started the fire, the IC must
contact law enforcement and report this involvement in a fire incident
report. The report should indicate that:
(1) The person involved in the ignition of the fire was a child or a
person under the age of 18.
(2) The fire was arson.
(3) The information known about the juvenile (e.g., name, age, sex,
address).
(4) The parent or guardian information, if known.
b) A copy of the report should be sent to the Fire Investigation Team
Division.
c) The IC should call a fire investigator any time there is evidence of arson,
when there are witnesses with information that could identify the
juvenile fire setter or when the suspect is still at the scene.
d) A juvenile who has been referred to the Department by the juvenile
justice court will be assigned to a member of the Fire Investigation Team
Division. If the juvenile fails to attend any mandated program sessions,
the Fire Investigation Team member should notify the court or the
juvenile’s probation officer. If the juvenile successfully attends all
required sessions and completes the program, the Fire Investigation
Team member should send a program completion letter on department
letterhead to the juvenile’s probation officer.
II. PROGRAM COMPONENTS
A. The following components should be included in any juvenile fire setter program.
Depending on the individual situation, some of the steps may not apply.
1. Assessment - The first step is generally a family interview including a Federal
Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) assessment at a location designated by
the Stickney Fire Department. Assessments may be conducted at the child’s home
or living environment of the child and family members are encouraged to attend.
2. Diversion - Diversion is a process that allows the child to complete all or some of
the program after which a citation can be dismissed or not processed. For
admission into diversion, the juvenile will undergo a criminal background check.
A parent or legal guardian and the child must attend a diversion hearing, where
the child will be asked to describe behaviors and to answer questions to assess

whether the child is at risk of repeating his/her offense. The child’s parents or
legal guardians and the child may be asked to sign a contract that requires specific
actions to qualify the child for continued participation in the program. When the
child successfully completes the program, the Department will process a request
to dismiss the citation.
3. Educational intervention - In this step, families attend a fire safety academy. It is
recommended that all family members attend. Academies may be conducted
several times throughout the year and child/family placement is subject to
availability. Academies should be broken into age- appropriate classes for the
juveniles. Informational training seminars should be included for parents and
guardians.
4. Counseling - The Department may recommend family counseling. If a child and
family have been referred to counseling, it is strongly recommended that the
counseling occur concurrently with academy attendance. A list of local
organizations and resources should be provided to the family.
5. Behavioral update - After completing the academy and/or counseling, a
representative from the fire setter program may follow up with adults in the
child’s home to discuss the child's behavior and review any progress.
B. The Fire Investigation Team Division should produce regular reports specific to juvenile
fire setters and outcomes. Reports should be included in department training programs
as part of awareness and disposition outcomes.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Fire Watch Services
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish guidance for the Department regarding incidents or situations
which may require a fire watch due to required automatic fire protection and/or detection services that
are inoperable, construction/demolition activities, hot work or other high-risk activities or events which
may have an adverse impact on public safety.
POLICY:
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department that the Department will, where required, ensure
appropriate measures are taken to protect building occupants, spectators or other attendees of certain
events pursuant to provisions of the Village fire code/ordinance.
I. DEFINITIONS
A. Fire guard - A person who is properly trained and whose sole duty is to patrol the premises
and watch for fire. This person should be equipped with an approved means of contacting
the Department in the event of a fire. Several fire guards might comprise a single fire
watch.
B. Fire watch - A temporary measure intended to ensure continuous and systematic
surveillance of a building or portion thereof by one or more qualified individuals for the
purposes of identifying and controlling fire hazards, detecting early signs of unwanted
fire, raising an alarm of fire and notifying the fire department. Fire watch may be
conducted by department personnel.
C. High life-risk occupancy - Hospitals, care facilities, schools, high-rise buildings and certain
assembly occupancies.
D. Hot work – Operations including cutting, welding, Thermit welding, brazing, soldering,
grinding, thermal spraying, thawing pipe, installation of torch-applied roof systems or any
other similar activity.
II. RESPONSIBILITIES
A. Upon notification that hot work activities are being performed or that required automatic
fire protection or detection systems are inoperable and the building or occupancy has not
been evacuated, the Fire Marshal or the authorized designee shall ensure that a fire watch
is implemented.

B. During special events or other activities, the Fire Marshal should make a determination
whether the location, premises, building or event has a high life-risk occupancy and, if so,
require or implement a fire watch. If the location does not have a high life-risk occupancy,
the Fire Marshal or the authorized designee shall evaluate each set of unique
circumstances and make a determination whether the property owner or event manager
shall implement a fire watch.
C. The following responsibilities apply for a fire watch:
1. The owner or the authorized designee shall immediately notify the Stickney Fire
Department any time an automatic fire protection or detection system is not in
operation.
2. Any repair or corrective action should be immediately initiated by the owner or
the authorized designee. After repair or corrective action is completed and the
system is back in service, the Stickney Fire Department and occupants should
again be notified by the owner or the authorized designee.
3. A fire watch should be provided when the system cannot be repaired in a timely
manner (more than 24 hours) and/or the lack of protection creates a building or
safety hazard as determined by the Fire Marshal or the authorized designee. A
fire watch shall be established immediately, however, when required fire
protection, detection and alarm systems are not in operation in high life-risk
occupancies, such as hospitals, care facilities, schools, high-rise buildings and
certain assembly occupancies.
4. Personnel used to conduct the fire watch are subject to the approval of the
Stickney Fire Department. The person performing fire watch duties shall have at
least one means of direct communication with the Stickney Fire Department and
his/her sole duty shall be to perform constant patrols and watch for the
occurrence of fire.
5. Building occupants must be notified within 24 hours of a fire watch being
established.
6. The minimum level of fire watch service shall be one fire guard per floor in multistory buildings and one fire guard for each fire protection system zone in a singlestory building. Additional fire guards may be needed, depending on the hazard
and building design. The fire watch service will continue until the automatic fire
protection or detection system is placed back in service. Fire guards shall be
provided with at least one approved means of notifying the Department and their
only duty shall be to perform constant patrols of the premises to watch for fires.
During the rounds, the fire watch personnel shall make a thorough inspection of
all buildings or spaces including concealed areas, such as attics, unoccupied
storage areas, etc.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Pre-Hospital Care Reports
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish the requirements for documentation of patient responses, and
the related document distribution, storage and disclosure pursuant to the Illinois Emergency Medical
Services Systems Act (210 ILCS 50/3.10 et seq.).
POLICY:
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to follow the patient documentation and distribution
guidelines developed by the local, regional or state EMS authority.
I. DEFINITIONS
A. Patient - A person who meets any one of the following criteria:
1. Has a chief complaint
2. Has obvious symptoms or signs of injury or illness
3. Has been involved in an event that the average Emergency Medical Responder
(EMR) would believe could cause an injury
4. Appears to be disoriented or to have impaired psychiatric function
5. Has evidence of suicidal intent
6. Is deceased
B. Patient Care Report and Pre-hospital Care Report (PCR) - Records regarding patient care
that are required by the Illinois Department of Public Health and/or the medical director
of a regional medical system (210 ILCS 50/3.195).
C. Patient refusing medical care against medical advice (AMA) - A competent patient who is
determined by a licensed emergency medical member (EMR, EMT, EMT-I, A-EMT, EMT-
P) or base hospital to have a medical problem that requires the immediate treatment
and/or transportation capabilities of the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) system, but
who declines medical care despite being advised of his/her condition and the risks and
possible complications of refusing medical care.

II. PROCEDURE
A. The Paramedic in charge of patient care shall be responsible for the accurate completion
and posting of the Patient Care Report (PCR).
B. A PCR shall be completed for every patient response. This includes a patient who is
released at the scene, meets the criteria for pronouncing death in the field, is an interfacility transport or is involved in a multi-casualty incident.
C. A PCR and a patient release form must be completed for all patients who refuse
evaluation, treatment and/or transport.
D. The senior Paramedic on the call shall ensure that a corresponding NFIRS report is
completed within FIREHOUSE Software®
E. The Lieutenant shall be responsible for obtaining any additional information or signatures
to complete the PCR and NFIRS report.
F. The Battalion Chief shall be responsible for ensuring that all PCRs are completed in a
timely manner and before the conclusion of the shift.
G. The PCR shall be completed immediately after transferring care at the receiving hospital
or returning back to the firehouse. A completed PCR shall be provided to the receiving
hospital before the ambulance leaves. When the ambulance must leave to respond to
another emergency call, the PCR will be returned to the hospital as soon as possible.
H. For continuous quality improvement, the local or regional EMS authority, department
EMS supervisors and the designated hospital receiving center shall review their copies of
the PCR and discuss any areas of concern.
III. DISTRIBUTION OF PCR COPIES
A. If a patient is transported to a hospital, copies should be distributed as follows:
1. Copy retained by the Department
2. Copy sent to the resource hospital
3. Copy left at the receiving hospital with the patient
B. If a patient is not transported or refuses care and leaves AMA, copies should be
distributed as follows:
1. Copy retained by the Department
2. Copy sent to the resource hospital
C. If a patient is declared dead and is not transported, copies should be distributed as
follows:
1. Copy retained by the Department
2. Copy sent to the resource hospital
3. Other copies sent per local EMS authority policy

IV. PCR STORAGE
A. All documentation received from the originating facility shall be listed in the PCR.
B. All completed PCRs and attached documents shall be forwarded to the Battalion Chief of
EMS or placed in a secure area designated for such reports.
C. The PCRs shall be maintained and secured in a manner consistent with the Patient
Medical Record Security and Privacy Policy.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Medical Supplies
body:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish a replenishment system for medical supply inventories for the
safety and welfare of patients and employees. Adequate accounting of inventory levels for ordering
medical supplies assist with budgeting and waste management. Adherence to this policy is intended to
prevent the depletion of protective supplies for employees and supplies for the treatment of patients,
while reducing inventory overstock and the inability to obtain critical supplies.
POLICY:
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department to replenish all medical supplies utilized during patient
treatment at the receiving hospital. Those supplies that are unable to be replenished at the receiving
hospital will be reported upon return to the station, via email, to the EMS Coordinator.
I. PROCEDURES
A. Each ambulance shall be fully inventoried weekly by the designated EMT assigned to the
ambulance to determine an adequate supply inventory. Those items that are missing and
cannot be replaced with stocked Stickney Fire Department inventory will be reported to
the EMS Coordinator via email.
B. Daily morning checks will be performed on the ambulances for designated targeted items.
C. Any member that utilizes the last of any stocked item shall notify the EMS Coordinator via
email.
II. MEDICATIONS
A. The following guidelines should be observed with regard to medication storage, security,
distribution and disposal:
1. Only department members who have received medication distribution training
may handle and distribute medications.
2. Medications shall be kept secure from unauthorized handling or use.
3. All medications should be inventoried daily by the designated EMT assigned to
the ambulance.
4. All medications should be kept in their original packaging.

5. All medications shall be protected from high temperatures by utilizing shaded
areas for prolonged parking of vehicles.
6. Medication packaging shall be protected to ensure the integrity of the medication
and that the lot numbers and expiration dates are legible.
7. Medications with expiration dates indicating only a month and year shall be
removed from the inventory on the last day of the month shown.
8. Near end date medications should be utilized first or exchanged for current
medications at the hospital when possible. Expired medications will be given to
the EMS Coordinator.
9. The Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Coordinator should provide direction to
members regarding the disposition of medications that are subject to product
alerts or recalls.
III. SUPPLY OVERSTOCK
A. Overstock should be returned to the EMS Coordinator.
B. Items should be properly packaged and labeled.
C. A written list of items being returned should be attached to the box or container with the
returned items.
D. Do not return individual items that are normally supplied as units in a case, bottle, or box.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief

title: Advance Health Care Directives
body:
PURPOSE:
This policy identifies the circumstances and types of documents required for department Emergency
Medical Services (EMS) members to withhold or withdraw resuscitative or life- sustaining measures based
on Illinois law (755 ILCS 40/65; 77 Ill. Adm. Code 515.380).
Nothing in this policy should be interpreted to limit EMS members from relieving an airway obstruction.
POLICY:
It is the policy of the Stickney Fire Department that EMS personnel honor valid DNR orders to withhold or
withdraw resuscitative measures (77 Ill. Adm. Code 515.380).
I. DEFINITIONS
A. Advance health care directive (or Advance Directive) - A document executed and used to
give health care instructions, including directions to withhold or withdraw life-sustaining
measures and CPR. A valid Advance Directive must contain the date of its execution, name
and signature of the attending physician, name of the patient, signature of the patient or
of another adult in the patient’s name, and the words “Do Not Resuscitate.”
B. EMS member - Members of the Department licensed as an Emergency Medical Technician
(EMT), Emergency Medical Technician-Intermediate (EMT-I), Advanced Emergency
Medical Technician (A-EMT) or Paramedic (EMT-P).
C. Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) order - A document that directs a health care provider not to
make resuscitative efforts, such as chest compressions, defibrillation, assisted ventilation,
basic airway adjuncts, advanced airway adjuncts (e.g., endotracheal tube, Combitube®),
cardiotonic medications or other medications or means intended to initiate a heartbeat
or to treat a non- perfusing rhythm. A DNR order includes:
1. An Illinois Department of Public Health Uniform Practitioner Orders for Life-
Sustaining Treatment (POLST) form.
2. Any other Advance Directive authorized under the regional EMS system policy. A
living will by itself is not a valid DNR order.
II. PROCEDURES
A. EMS members shall honor a DNR order when it can be reasonably established that the
patient is the subject of the DNR order and either:

1. When EMS members have identified a DNR order as defined in this policy.
2. When EMS members have personally seen the DNR order in the patient’s medical
record in a health care facility and they reasonably believe it has not been
revoked.
B. DNR patients should receive non-resuscitation-related palliative care and other comfort
measures, as would any other person.
C. A DNR order shall be disregarded if the patient orders resuscitative measures.
D. When EMS members honor a DNR order, they should note on the Pre-Hospital Care
Report (PCR) that a DNR order was presented and honored and shall document the
circumstances surrounding the DNR order on the PCR. (See SFD Policy 500)
E. Resource hospital contact should be made, the resource hospital physician consulted and
resuscitation initiated:
1. If there are any questions concerning the validity of the DNR order.
2. If a DNR order is incomplete or not signed.
3. When a document other than those noted in this policy is presented.
4. Any time EMS members have concerns or require assistance.
F. DNR patients who are in cardiopulmonary arrest should not be transported unless
required by the resource hospital. EMS members shall contact local law enforcement
and/or the coroner’s office to report the death and should support family members onscene, as appropriate.
G. DNR patients who decline transport to the hospital, including patients for whom transport
is declined on their behalf, should not be transported. EMS members should make
reasonable efforts to preserve the patient’s privacy, dignity and comfort before leaving
the scene.
H. If a DNR patient is transported to a hospital, the following shall apply:
1. A valid DNR order shall be honored during transport of the patient.
2. The DNR order shall accompany the patient.
3. The attorney-in-fact or health care agent (if applicable) should accompany the
patient to the hospital.
I. Members shall also follow any requirements in any regional EMS system policies related
to DNR orders.
By Order of:
Jeff Boyajian
Fire Chief
